title: Harry and Meghan’s security funding on UK return is private matter, Burnham says
author: Caroline Davies
content:
Security arrangements for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex while living in the UK are a “private matter”, Andy Burnham has said, after news that Harry and Meghan intend to relocate to Britain from the US this month.
The UK prime minister refused to be drawn on security funding, saying: “This is a private matter. It’s a matter for Harry and Meghan, and we wish them well in the moves that they’re making.”
The couple, who moved to North America more than six years ago, will make their home in a non-royal residence outside London. Their children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, are already enrolled at British schools and due to start in September.
King Charles, who was told of the decision on Sunday, is said to welcome the opportunity to see more of his family in a personal capacity. There will be no change in their status as private individuals and non-working royals who do not carry out royal engagements. There is said to be no half-in, half-out option.
Security funding has been a long-running source of tension between Harry and the Home Office, the government department that would decide on such measures. The Times has reported that there are no plans to provide the couple and their family with taxpayer-funded armed protection.
Last year, Harry lost a protracted court battle over what security he and his family would be entitled to while visiting the UK after automatic taxpayer-funded security was withdrawn when the couple stood down as working royals.
During the legal challenge against the Home Office, Harry said in his witness statement: “The UK is my home. The UK is central to the heritage of my children and a place I want them to feel at home as much as where they live at the moment in the US. That cannot happen if it’s not possible to keep them safe when they are on UK soil. I cannot put my wife in danger like that and, given my experiences in life, I am reluctant to unnecessarily put myself in harm’s way too.”
A senior judge later ruled that his “sense of grievance” over the decision about his security was not sufficient as grounds for an appeal.
The prince later told the BBC that he “can’t see a world” in which he would bring his family to the UK.
He was understood to be already awaiting a fresh risk-management assessment, but his new circumstances may now have to be factored in. Decisions on the security of royals are taken by the royal and VIP executive committee, an independent body overseen by the Home Office. The prime minister does not decide about security for the royal family.
After the couple left the UK, Harry was granted a “bespoke” security arrangement. He may no longer qualify for the level of protection he previously had as a working royal but he is a high-profile figure and former military serviceman who has served in Afghanistan, which may be considered in any assessment.
A Home Office spokesperson said: “The UK government’s protective security system is rigorous and proportionate. It is our long-standing policy not to provide detailed information on those arrangements, as doing so could compromise their integrity and affect individuals’ security.”
In the US, the Sussexes paid for their own private security team.
![Prince Harry and Meghan react to a crowd of people taking photos of the couple on their phones](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/50433cc3f085face8b2018017b5f18395137cfb5/0_0_6000_4001/master/6000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
There has been no statement from the Sussexes on why they are choosing to return to the UK, but a source close to them said they had had a great time during their visit in July, and that “stars are aligning with work” to make this a good time to move. This may include Harry’s Invictus Games, which are to be held in Birmingham next year.
The couple intend to retain their properties in Montecito, California, and in Portugal. Meghan is expected to run her lifestyle brand As Ever from the UK, but it is not yet known whether she will begin undertaking charity visits as a non-working royal or embark on other ventures.
Harry has recently made it clear that he would like to spend more time with his father, who has cancer. Next year also marks the 30th anniversary of the death of his mother, Diana, which will include commemorations and events in the UK. Harry and his family stayed at home of Diana’s family, the Spencers, in Althorp, Northamptonshire, during their visit to the UK last month.
A YouGov poll of 5,810 adults carried out the day after the Sussex’s surprise news, showed 33% believe Harry and Meghan should not return to the UK, while 45% do not know. Less than a quarter (21%) are in favour of the Sussexes relocating to the UK.
summary: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex intend to relocate from the US to a non-royal residence outside London this month, with their children enrolled in British schools starting in September. Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that security arrangements are a private matter, while reports indicate there are no plans to provide taxpayer-funded armed protection. King Charles reportedly welcomes the move, though the couple will remain private individuals and non-working royals without a half-in, half-out option.
key_points: Harry and Meghan plan to relocate back to the UK from the US with their children.
The UK prime minister stated that security funding for the couple is a private matter.
Reports indicate there are no plans to provide taxpayer-funded armed protection for the family.
The couple will retain their status as private individuals and non-working royals.
King Charles was informed of the decision and welcomes the opportunity to see more of his family.

title: Harry and Meghan: the key moments, conflicts and controversies since their US move
author: Guardian staff reporter
content:
Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, will reportedly return to Britain after six years of living in the US, a move that triggered a long period of strained relations with King Charles III, the Prince and Princess of Wales and others in the royal family.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their two children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, are expected to relocate to the UK this month.
The family will reportedly live at a private, non-royal residence outside London, but they plan to maintain their home in California and another property in Portugal.
Here is a timeline charting the major moments since the family moved to the US in 2020.
2020
January
Harry and Meghan announce they will step down as working royals. The decision comes after a period marked by open warfare with the media over claimed intrusion and bullying.
“We intend to step back as ‘senior’ members of the royal family and work to become financially independent, while continuing to fully support Her Majesty the Queen,” the couple say.
June
The couple moves to Meghan’s native California, settling in the wealthy seaside enclave of Montecito near Santa Barbara. Media reports put the 2020 purchase price of their 16-bedroom home at $14.7m.
2021
March
Harry and Meghan are interviewed by Oprah Winfrey on CBS.
In a series of stunning revelations, Meghan accuses the royal family of fostering an atmosphere of racial hostility so intense that she came close to suicide while pregnant with Archie. Meghan also claims members of the royal family had openly expressed concerns about how dark Archie’s skin would be.
In response, Queen Elizabeth issues a statement: “The issues raised, particularly that of race, are concerning. While some recollections may vary, they are taken very seriously and will be addressed by the family privately.”
![Prince Harry and Meghan are interviewed by Oprah Winfrey](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5edd035b0acac397640f40589f799e9945762ffb/0_0_3500_2627/master/3500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
June
The couple’s second child, Lilibet, is born in California. She is named after the family nickname for the Queen.
2022
August
Harry files a lawsuit against the Home Office and the Metropolitan police over his security arrangements in the UK since he stepped down as a working royal.
September
While Harry and Meghan are visiting London, Queen Elizabeth dies. They stay in Britain for her funeral. Ahead of the funeral, Harry and Meghan join William and Kate in meeting wellwishers outside Windsor castle.
![Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, attend the state funeral and burial of Queen Elizabeth](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/1158b4c9e21b3f552cfb23a1dfb032821e161b2b/0_0_4576_3074/master/4576.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
2023
January
Harry publishes his memoir Spare, detailing his relationship with his family.
Among the most notable revelations, Harry recounts what he says was a physical attack by William as their relationship fell apart over his marriage to Meghan. Describing a confrontation at his London home in 2019, Harry says William called Meghan “difficult”, “rude” and “abrasive”.
May
Harry attends his father’s coronation alone after Meghan and his young children opted not to attend and to remain in California. He walks into Westminster Abbey alone and is seated two rows behind William.
![Prince Harry at the coronation ceremony of King Charles III in Westminster Abbey](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/456937fe5376fa01de79b121c59174bde6c9eed5/0_0_6000_4000/master/6000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
![Prince Harry departs Westminster Abbey during the Coronation of King Charles](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b710c127ff23fb0f5fe5b1f0539c76bfdefeae6f/0_0_5732_3822/master/5732.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
2024
February
Buckingham Palace announces King Charles has been diagnosed with a form of cancer and will postpone public engagements to undergo treatment. Harry is photographed arriving at his father’s London residence for a brief meeting.
2025
April
Appearing at a high court appeal over the changes to his police protection, Harry’s lawyer warns his “life is at stake”. The Home Office, defending the appeal, says that Harry’s “bespoke” security arrangements are designed to accommodate his “unique set of circumstances”.
May
Harry loses the legal challenge over his security arrangements, allowing the government to proceed with a “bespoke”, and cheaper, level of protection for his family. Three senior judges reject Harry’s claim he had been “singled out” for “inferior treatment”.
Later that same day, Harry says he wants reconciliation with his family, explaining that his father no longer speaks to him due to the security row.
Speaking in California, Harry says: “I can’t see a world in which I would be bringing my wife and children back to the UK at this point … I miss the UK. And it’s really quite sad I won’t be able to show my children my homeland.”
August
Harry and Meghan sign a fresh deal with Netflix. The couple, who struck a five-year deal in 2020 reportedly worth $100m (£78m), had collaborated with Netflix on a number of projects. Media reports had suggested that poor viewing figures for some of the projects meant that Netflix would not extend the deal.
![Harry and Meghan on a Netflix show](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7d0ab19bfa3f0ba7619134002faf68f442846c91/404_24_1961_1307/master/1961.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
2026
June
Buckingham Palace says Harry will not be staying at the palace during a visit to London, despite the Duke of Sussex’s team earlier announcing publicly he had accepted an invitation to do so.
July
Harry and other high-profile British figures lose their privacy lawsuits against the Daily Mail’s publisher. Harry and the group face a legal bill of up to £50m after losing their case.
![Prince Harry arrives at the Royal Courts of Justice in London](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/35b8b876fc218baf5a79485d8f195a0f896855f9/0_0_4996_3546/master/4996.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
July
King Charles meets in private with Harry and his family, having not seen the children for four years. According to reports, Harry, Meghan, Archie and Lilibet were hosted by Charles and Queen Camilla at the king’s private residence in Gloucestershire.
August
The couple reportedly plan to move with Archie and Lilibet from California to Britain for an extended period. The children will begin school there in September, but the couple will not return to royal duties, according to reports.
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are reportedly planning to relocate from California back to Britain with their two children after six years of living in the US. Their move follows a turbulent period marked by strained relations with the royal family, legal battles over security, and media controversies. Despite returning to the UK to live at a private residence, they plan to maintain their properties in California and Portugal and will not return to working royal duties.
key_points: Prince Harry and Meghan are reportedly moving back to Britain with their children after six years in the US.
The family will live at a private residence outside London while maintaining homes in California and Portugal.
Their time in the US was marked by major conflicts, including a 2021 Oprah interview alleging racism and Harry's 2023 memoir detailing family rifts.
Harry lost a legal challenge regarding his UK security arrangements and faced setbacks in privacy lawsuits against the Daily Mail's publisher.
King Charles met privately with Harry, Meghan, and their children in July 2026, marking a step toward reconciliation after years of strained relations.

title: BBC DJ Trevor Nelson reveals brain tumour surgery 'went well'
author: Yasmin Rufo
content:
![Trevor Nelson attends night 4 of the "Usher: Past Present Future" tour at The O2 Arena on April 05, 2025 in London, England](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/636/cpsprodpb/85e4/live/9e515620-9caa-11f1-84cf-fd4cfd9d6c84.jpg)
- Published
BBC DJ and presenter Trevor Nelson has revealed he stepped away from work after being diagnosed with a brain tumour.
Nelson was last on air in June and had announced he was "taking a little break from my work commitments" due to "health issues".
Speaking to his Instagram followers, external, the 62-year-old said that his "world was turned upside down" when a brain tumour was discovered.
He said that he had undergone a "very serious surgery" which "went incredibly well".
Speaking on Instagram on Thursday, Nelson explained: "There's been a lot of speculation as to what's wrong with me, I know that much. My phone's blown up 20 times over with people asking what's wrong with me.
"I felt that I should at least tell you what was wrong with me. I'm not going to go into it all now and I will deep dive into it at a later date so you can hear the full story."
He continued: "I'll tell you this, I was minding my own business and then it was discovered I had a brain tumour.
"I was shocked, my world was turned upside down, it was a shock to myself and close family and friends and you can imagine quite literally my head was all over the place."
'Feel great right now'
He reassured fans his surgery went well and last month has "been at home, recuperating, recovering and resting and getting some post-op treatment as well".
He added that he feels "great right now" and "ready to come back".
"I feel energised and almost back to myself, yes I've had a really serious situation but I've come out the other side at this point and I feel great. I feel raring to go and I feel in good health."
Dan Knowles, chief executive at the charity Brain Tumour Research, external, said: "Every day, 35 people are diagnosed with a brain tumour.
"We thank Trevor for sharing his diagnosis and treatment, helping to raise awareness of this disease and the impact it has on families across the UK. We are thinking of him and wishing him well as he navigates this journey."
The father-of-two said he is back to doing things he enjoys like playing golf and going to the gym.
He urged fans not to worry about him and thanked everyone for their love and support.
Nelson, who presents a weekday afternoon show on Radio 2 and appears on 1Xtra late on a Sunday morning, celebrated 30 years at the BBC earlier this year.
![Trevor Nelson performs as part of BBC Radio 1Xtra's DJ Relay Marathon World Record attempt at Vibe Bar on June 5, 2010 in London, England](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/2283/live/c2675000-9caa-11f1-84cf-fd4cfd9d6c84.jpg)
Nelson, pictured here in 2010, has been working with the BBC since 1996
His colleagues, including from former Radio 2 presenter Zoe Ball, wished him well and Ball said it is "so good to see your face and learn that you're doing well".
DJ Clara Amfo praised his "brilliant surgeons" and sent him love as did comedian Romesh Ranganathan who wrote on Instagram: "much love legend".
The Brain Tumour Charity also commented on his Instagram video and thanked Nelson for sharing his diagnosis.
"We are thinking of you and your loved ones during this time. We're always here if you need support or someone to talk to."
Nelson started his career at Kiss FM in London and after 10 years he moved to Radio 1 in 1996 to present Rhythm Nation.
He also worked in television, presenting MTV's black music shows The Lick and The Lick Chart before hosting his own shows on the BBC like Trevor Nelson's Urban Choice and The Lowdown.
In 2002, Nelson received an MBE for his contribution to the Millennium Volunteers programme.
summary: BBC DJ and presenter Trevor Nelson has revealed that he stepped away from work after being diagnosed with a brain tumour. He shared on Instagram that he underwent a very serious surgery, which went incredibly well, and has been recovering at home. Nelson stated that he now feels great, energised, and ready to return to his work commitments.
key_points: Trevor Nelson stepped away from his BBC broadcasting duties in June due to health issues.
The 62-year-old DJ revealed he was diagnosed with a brain tumour, which required serious surgery.
Nelson confirmed on Instagram that his post-op surgery went well and he has been recuperating at home.
He stated he feels great, energised, and ready to return to normal activities such as playing golf and going to the gym.
The chief executive of Brain Tumour Research thanked Nelson for sharing his diagnosis to help raise awareness.

title: DEA Joins Hayden Panettiere's Death Investigation: Report

Greenville police “accompanied by EMS personnel, responded to a report of an unresponsive female” on Sunday (Aug. 16), according to a statement given to NBC News. “Upon arrival, medical assistance was administered; however, the individual, later identified as Hayden Panettiere, was pronounced deceased at the scene.”

Panettiere had long been candid about her struggles navigating child stardom and the rampant sexual harassment and abuse in the entertainment industry. In the book, the star detailed her prolific and sometimes difficult career in show business; growing up under the harsh light of Hollywood; and the highs and lows of filming hit TV shows like Heroes and Nashville, and more.
summary: The Drug Enforcement Administration has joined the investigation into the death of actress Hayden Panettiere, assisting the lead agency, the Greenville City Police Department. title: Sandra Bullock speaks out about partner’s ‘traumatic’ death for first time
author: Tom Murray
content:
Sandra Bullock is opening up about the loss of her longtime partner, Bryan Randall, for the first time since his death in August 2023.
Randall — a model-turned-photographer — met Bullock in 2015 after she hired him to photograph her son Louis’ fifth birthday party. He was diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in 2020.
ALS is a progressive nervous system disease in which the brain gradually loses its connection with the muscles, taking away a person’s ability to walk, talk, eat and, eventually, breathe. There is currently no cure or treatment that halts progression.
Bullock, 62, recalled the “traumatic diagnosis” in the forthcoming episode of the Smartless podcast, which is currently available to SiriusXM early access subscribers.
“I wasn’t allowed to speak about it. That was [his] request and I tried — I honored it,” Bullock told hosts Jason Bateman, Will Arnett and Sean Hayes.
![Bullock’s partner of eight years, Bryan Randall, died in 2023 — three years after he was diagnosed with ALS](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/20/7/33/GettyImages-968036122.jpeg)
“My sister [Gesine Bullock-Prado] was the only one who knew for a while.”
Bullock admitted that the secrecy “isolated me in the process” amid the Covid-19 pandemic while carrying the “huge weight” of his diagnosis.
Bullock said she told herself, “Oh, I can handle that. I can be quiet.” But caring for Randall while raising her two young children during the pandemic ultimately became “a trifecta that was pretty dark,” she said.
She eventually shared what was happening with her friends Jennifer Aniston and Bateman’s wife, Amanda.
“I think where he was in his journey, both physically and mentally, I started grieving Bryan four years before he passed,” Bullock said. “There was something that had shifted.”
“My person left a lot earlier than the body left,” Practical Magic 2 star continued. “I don’t think I ever dealt with that until after he passed, because you’re just on this treadmill.”
The actor and Randall co-parented her son, Louis, and daughter, Laila, as well as Randall’s daughter from a previous relationship, Skylar Staten Randall.
ALS has received heightened public attention in recent years following a number of high-profile diagnoses and deaths.
Grey’s Anatomy and Euphoria star Eric Dane died earlier this year from the disease after what his family called “a courageous battle with ALS.” In the months before his death, he raised awareness of the condition, even playing a firefighter with ALS on NBC’s Brilliant Minds.
In May, Russell Andrews, a veteran actor who appeared in major shows like Better Call Saul and Grey’s Anatomy, shared his diagnosis with ALS.
“Receiving this diagnosis changed my life,” Andrews said via ALS Network. “What I didn’t expect was the depth of connection and support that comes with it. There’s a community here that shows up in ways that matter.”
Bullock’s episode of SmartLess will be available on all podcast platforms on August 24.
summary: Sandra Bullock has spoken out for the first time about the 2023 death of her longtime partner, Bryan Randall, who passed away following a secret three-year battle with ALS. In an upcoming podcast episode, she revealed that keeping his diagnosis private during the COVID-19 pandemic left her feeling isolated while she cared for him and raised her children. Bullock explained that she began grieving Randall years before his physical death because the disease had already changed him.
key_points: Sandra Bullock discussed Bryan Randall's death from ALS for the first time in a podcast appearance.
Randall was diagnosed with ALS in 2020, and at his request, the diagnosis was kept largely secret.
Bullock stated that maintaining the secrecy and caring for Randall during the pandemic while raising children was a dark and isolating experience.
She shared that she began grieving Randall years before his actual passing due to the toll of the disease.

title: Josh Radnor Is ‘Not Even a Little Bit’ Close to His ‘How I Met Your Mother’ Co-Stars: ‘You Just Go Out and Live Your Life’
author: Jack Dunn
content:
Josh Radnor recently told the “Half the Picture” podcast that he is “not even a little bit” close to his “How I Met Your Mother” co-stars, despite filming together for 208 episodes across 9 seasons.
When asked if he’s still tight with his “How I Met Your Mother” family, Radnor said, “No. Not even a little bit.”
He explained, “I don’t mean that in any dramatic way. It’s just… We had Neil [Patrick Harris] on the podcast, and he and I had a really interesting conversation about some of the tension we had on set that was fascinating and kind of healing.”
Popular on Variety
Radnor hosts a “HIMYM” rewatch podcast with series co-creator Craig Thomas. Harris appeared on an episode earlier in 2026.
He explained that he and Jason Segel “send each other texts every once in a while,” but he hasn’t seen him in “a really long time.” As for Cobie Smulders, who’s been on his podcast a few times, he’s “seen her mostly on Zoom.” Radnor recalled seeing Alyson Hannigan last at his wedding in 2024.
“I have love for all these people,” Radnor said. “It’s like college where you have this very intense time together, and you think you’re going to be — you can’t imagine not seeing each other every day because you’ve seen each other every day for so long. And then it just disperses, and you just go out and live your life.”
He continued, “I think it’s a little more like family than friends in that you don’t get to choose your family. We were cast. We didn’t choose each other. And family dynamics come out to play when you’re in an environment like that for so long. But you also have love that is quite deep and rich and probably everlasting, but it’s not an active love. Acting is like love affairs that you have, and then you move on.”
summary: Actor Josh Radnor revealed on a podcast that he is not close to his "How I Met Your Mother" co-stars despite filming nine seasons together. He compared the cast dynamic to family or college, noting that while he still has deep affection for them, they have all moved on with their lives. Radnor does maintain minimal contact with some cast members, such as occasional texts with Jason Segel and virtual interactions with Cobie Smulders.
key_points: Josh Radnor stated he is not close to his "How I Met Your Mother" co-stars.
Radnor and co-star Neil Patrick Harris recently had a healing conversation about past on-set tension during an episode of Radnor's rewatch podcast.
Radnor occasionally texts Jason Segel and has interacted with Cobie Smulders via Zoom.
Alyson Hannigan last attended Radnor's wedding in 2024.
Radnor compared the cast's relationship to a family where members are cast together rather than choosing one another.

title: Rob Rinder announces dad’s death aged 73 after being diagnosed with illness
author: Milo Pope

![](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEC_308884273-cc6a.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Rob Rinder has revealed that his dad has died at the age of 73 after being diagnosed with an illness that has been ‘desperately under-researched’.
The author, TV judge and criminal barrister, shared the news with his followers that David Rinder, who worked as a London black cab driver for over 40 years, has died.
David had been living with Lewy body dementia, leading Rob to become a vocal patron and advocate for the Lewy Body Society to raise awareness for the condition.
Writing on Instagram, Rob wrote: ‘My dad died yesterday aged 73. I wasn’t sure whether to share this but if it brings attention to an illness too few people understand, perhaps it belongs here.
‘A London cabbie & lifelong Spurs supporter, he was there for every one of my brothers’ and grandsons’ football matches. I once represented him at the Carriage Office for bad driving; I loved him but the prosecution had a case…’
Rob, who is also known for his work presenting documentaries and co-hosting travel shows with Rylan Clark, said that his parents divorced when he was young, so he did not grow up with his dad at home.
![](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/GettyImages-497910810-2067-e1777736062989.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
‘We were very different men. I loved opera and all its drama; he loved Tottenham and cigarettes. We both took people as we found them and we both loved women, though in rather different ways.
‘I never once doubted his pride in me. When I came out he responded with magnificent indifference: I was still his son, there was nothing else to discuss.’
Rob praised the work of Jewish Care which became his dad’s home and ‘a place where dignity and tenderness were practised every day’.
‘A Jewish man, held in his final days by people of different faiths: a quiet reminder that what is sacred in us is also what we share. He died with his family around him loved and held to the last,’ he added.
What is Lewy Body dementia?
Lewy body dementia is a type of progressive dementia that causes trouble with thinking, movement, sleep and behaviour.
Sharing symptoms with both Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s, the brain disease is caused by abnormal deposits of a protein called alpha-synuclein building up in the brain. These deposits are called Lewy bodies.
One of the biggest differences between Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body dementia is that memory loss isn’t always the first or most prominent symptom.
With the former, problems with attention, alertness, visual perception and movement can appear early, while memory can fluctuate.
‘Funny, beautifully flawed, loving and my dad. Lewy body dementia took him far too young.

title: Prince Harry and Meghan's UK security a private matter, Burnham says

Prince Harry and Meghan are planning to move back to the UK, BBC News understands
- Published
Security arrangements for The Duke and Duchess of Sussex on their return to the UK are a "private matter," Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said.
He added: "It's a matter for Harry and for Meghan, and we wish them well in the move that they are making."
It comes after it emerged that the couple intend to relocate with their children from the US to the UK later this month to a private, non-royal residence outside London.
Security for the couple has long been a point of tension, with Prince Harry losing a legal challenge last year over the levels of security he and his family are entitled to while in the UK.
The couple's children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, are enrolled to start at a British school in September.
King Charles was told of the move on Sunday. There are no current plans for either Prince Harry or Meghan to resume their roles as working royals.
The Sussexes left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year.
They were last in the UK in July to visit the King and Queen Camilla, in what was seen as a key development in their relationship.
The Palace described the meeting at the King's private home in Gloucestershire as a "private family occasion".
It was the first time the King had seen his grandchildren in person in more than four years, and the couple's first visit to the UK together since 2022.
It is understood that July's visit had to be adjusted after the duke's request for police protection was rejected.
Last year, Prince Harry lost a legal challenge in which he sought to overturn a decision that had downgraded his security after his move to the US.
At the time, he told the BBC that he "can't see a world" in which he would bring his family to the UK due to the downgrading of his protection.
It is unclear what provisions will be made for their security once they return to the UK.
Royal expert Robert Hardman told the BBC's Radio 4 Today programme it was likely that some of their past security issues "have been resolved" but details - or who is going to foot the bill - are still unknown.

title: Can Pirates of the Caribbean 6 save Johnny Depp’s career – or is he damaged goods?
author: Louis Chilton
content:
Is it a sixth voyage on the seven seas for Johnny Depp? According to superproducer Jerry Bruckheimer, the controversial American actor is in talks to reprise the role of Captain Jack Sparrow in a new Pirates of the Caribbean movie – a deal that would herald a full-on Hollywood comeback for Depp after half a decade in the cinematic wilderness.
During court proceedings in 2022, Depp testified that Disney had dropped him from the Pirates franchise, claiming that he would refuse to rejoin the series even if he were offered “$300m and a million alpacas”. While it’s not known how much money – or indeed how many alpacas – Disney may or may not be willing to offer him, the assumption among many is that a return could be very much on the cards. (Orlando Bloom, who fronted the original Pirates trilogy in the 2000s alongside Depp and Keira Knightley, hinted last year that he was interested in a reboot.)
Talk of a sixth Pirates of the Caribbean film comes weeks after the first trailer debuted for Depp’s other “comeback” project, an adaptation of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol. “It’s good to be back,” whispers Johnny Depp, in the meta-referential first trailer for Ebenezer. The film, out later this year, isn’t Depp’s first foray into cinema since his highly publicised, career-derailing legal battle with ex-wife Amber Heard, but it is his first back in the Hollywood system.
While no one but the Ghost of Christmas Future can be sure of Ebenezer’s fortunes, Bruckheimer’s comments are the strongest suggestion yet that studios are ready to re-embrace Depp. Back in the shabby pirate garb of Captain Jack, Depp would be reprising the biggest role of his career. Are the public on board? It seems that studios are ready to start betting on it.
![Depp as Jack Sparrow in ‘Pirates of the Caribbean’](https://static.the-independent.com/2025/08/13/07/newFile-1.jpg)
For Depp, a sixth Pirates film would be a return to the franchise that made him a bankable blockbuster star after spending years struggling to crack the mainstream. As shambling, sauntering pirate-with-a-heart-of-gold Jack Sparrow, Depp created for himself an inimitable breakout character; audiences loved him, and so did critics. (It was Pirates that won Depp his first Oscar nomination.)
The magnitude and turbulence of Depp’s 21st-century fame make it easy to forget that he started out as a teen pin-up, thanks to his role in the TV hit 21 Jump Street – and Hollywood success was initially elusive. The 1980s and 1990s saw him work with a slew of lauded filmmakers – among them Wes Craven (in Depp’s debut film, the horror classic A Nightmare on Elm Street), John Waters (in Cry-Baby), and Terry Gilliam (in Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas). He produced much of his best work in collaboration with Tim Burton – as the Chaplinesque monster in Edward Scissorhands, and the titular schlock filmmaker in Ed Wood.
Many of these films, however, were box office bombs. Depp was an actor with arthouse cachet, but no mainstream bankability; he was arguably best known at the time for his string of glamorous off-camera romances (with actors including Jennifer Grey, Sherilyn Fenn and Winona Ryder, and the model Kate Moss).
“I went through 20 years of what the industry basically described as failures,” Depp said, at a 2009 press conference. “For 20 years I was defined as box office poison.”
When he landed the lead part in Burton’s Sleepy Hollow (1999), his biggest pre-Pirates hit, it was as a last resort; while the director had wanted Depp from the get-go, Paramount pushed a number of other names (Brad Pitt; Liam Neeson; Daniel Day-Lewis) before accepting. Dreamy France-set romance Chocolat was another success the following year, making $152.7m, more than six times its budget.
![Johnny Depp as Ichabod Crane in ‘Sleepy Hollow’](https://static.the-independent.com/2024/07/11/11/07_SleepyHollow.jpg)
Then in 2003 came Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl. Adapted from a long-running theme park ride, the film was widely expected to be a commercial disaster, but ended up a juggernaut: the first film made $650m (£478m). Over the next four entries (released across the span of 14 years), the franchise would go on to make more than $4.5bn from box office takings alone, with Depp’s shabby sea captain quickly promoted from a supporting role to the undeniable star attraction.
Disney may have reason to believe there’s treasure buried somewhere within a hypothetical sixth Pirates film: the most recent entry, released in the UK as Pirates of the Caribbean: Salazar’s Revenge, made just shy of $795.9m, despite poor reviews and a cast switch-up. (Bloom and Knightley left after the third entry, with only Geoffrey Rush remaining of the main cast – Penelope Cruz and Javier Bardem were the star additions for the fourth and fifth films respectively.)
A major point of contention in the Depp v Heard court case was that Heard’s allegations of domestic abuse – which Depp claimed were defamatory and false – had jeopardised his career. (A jury in Virginia ultimately ruled in Depp’s favour, awarding him damages.) A previous British court ruling over The Sun report labelling him a “wife beater” had immediately precipitated his firing from another major franchise, the Harry Potter spin-off series Fantastic Beasts; taking the stand in 2022, his manager stated that Disney had nixed a prospective $22.5m deal to bring him back to the Pirates franchise. If they are now willing to reverse that decision, it suggests a significant sea change – either with regard to Depp himself, or the public’s willingness to overlook his scandals.
What cachet Depp has retained through the reputation-damaging trial is uncertain. Polling by the National Research Group earlier this year placed Depp seventh in a ranking of actors who would most convince respondents to watch a film. “I do see a path for him, particularly because Hollywood needs this comeback,” Miranda Banks, a professor of film, television and media studies at LA’s Loyola Marymount University, recently told The New York Times. “There’s an incredible lack of compelling A-listers who can open movies on a worldwide basis.”
The dearth of viable movie stars – actors who can, in industry terms, “open a movie” on their own appeal – is a documented modern phenomenon, despite the ascendence of young box office draws such as Timothée Chalamet and Zendaya. Disney may be influenced by the success of actors such as Brad Pitt, who last year marked his highest-grossing movie ever (Apple TV’s racing drama F1) despite myriad headlines about his personal life and abuse allegations from ex-wife Angelina Jolie. (Pitt has consistently denied the abuse allegations.) It may be that audiences don’t know; it may be that they don’t care.
Since the trial, Depp has appeared in just two films. The first is the 2023 French-language drama Jeanne du Barry. (The film’s director, Maïwenn, spoke positively of Depp in a 2023 interview with The Independent, though claimed: “It’s difficult to shoot with him... all the crew were scared because he has a different kind of humour and we didn’t know if he was going to be on time, or if he was going to be OK to say his lines.”) The second is a 2024 children’s film titled Johnny Puff: Secret Mission, in which Depp provides noises – but not words – for an animated puffin. It’s a reprisal of a role he played in 70 episodes of the Apple TV+ series Puffins a few years prior.
To this end, Ebenezer is an unlikely lifeline; another Pirates outing would constitute a comeback of tremendous magnitude. But studios have reasons for caution that go beyond Depp’s damaged personal reputation. Across the 2010s, Depp’s success with the Pirates franchise was tempered by a slew of ignominious box-office flops – among them the woozy Bruce Robinson jaunt The Rum Diary (2010), errant adventure throwback The Lone Ranger (2013), and the woeful comedy Mortdecai (2015). Though his reputation as a box-office draw was sustained through his work as Jack Sparrow (and other sporadic successes like Alice in Wonderland and Murder on the Orient Express), Depp’s allure was demonstrably faltering long before he was supposedly “cancelled”.
With nine years having passed since the last Pirates film, the world’s enduring fascination with the exploits of Captain Sparrow are a matter of pure conjecture. Even leaving aside Depp’s personal appeal, it’s uncertain whether the moment has passed. These are, after all, family films, and those people who were the prime age demographic when the last film came out have now grown up. It’s no surprise the sixth film is being talked of as a reboot (with the rumoured involvement of Margot Robbie as the lead). It will inevitably seek to split the difference – courting an audience of children unfamiliar with Depp, while appealing to those adult fans who grew up with him.
It is unlikely that such a film wouldn’t, at the very least, be profitable. But the bigger question is whether Depp can endure without the idiosyncratic draw of Jack Sparrow. If Depp was once “box office poison”, Captain Jack proved to be his antidote. Whether it will work again remains to be seen.
summary: Superproducer Jerry Bruckheimer has indicated that Johnny Depp is in talks to reprise his role as Captain Jack Sparrow in a sixth Pirates of the Caribbean movie. This potential deal suggests that major Hollywood studios are ready to re-embrace Depp following his career-derailing legal battles and public controversies. While a return to his most famous franchise would mark a major comeback, industry experts note that Depp also faced numerous box office flops prior to his controversies.
key_points: Producer Jerry Bruckheimer stated that Johnny Depp is in talks to return as Captain Jack Sparrow in a new Pirates of the Caribbean film.
Depp previously testified that Disney dropped him from the franchise during his 2022 legal proceedings with ex-wife Amber Heard.
Depp's upcoming adaptation of A Christmas Carol, titled Ebenezer, marks his first project back within the Hollywood system since his legal trials.
Despite past controversies and box office flops in the 2010s, studios may be willing to gamble on Depp due to a current scarcity of global A-list movie stars.

![Brooklyn insists he is happier with his wife now that he's distanced himself from his family (Jerod Harris/Getty Images)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHQ5YTA4M2JlZTQwOTdhNDJhLzZhODZhMWIxZTQ5Zjg4OTk3YmU0NzAxMC9icm9va2x5bi1iZWNraGFtLW5pY29sYS1wZWx0ei1sYXRlc3QuanBn.webp)
However, a recent shirtless picture on Instagram showed that the tribute to his mother was now completely covered up.
It has been replaced by a floral bouquet from the couple's wedding back in 2022, while another selfie revealed that his anchor tribute to David is also faded and barely visible, with a number of small cover-ups.

Although things have turned sour, it seems as if the aspiring chef is more than happy with the decision he made.
![What the tattoo looked like before (LADbible/brooklynpeltzbeckham/Instagram)](https://resizer.ladbiblegroup.com/unsafe/rs:fit:3840:0:0:0/g:sm/q:70/aHR0cHM6Ly9ldS1pbWFnZXMuY29udGVudHN0YWNrLmNvbS92My9hc3NldHMvYmx0Y2Q3NGFjYzFkMGE5OWYzYS9ibHQ5OTM2MTExNjY1MWY5MGExLzZhODZiMzI2ZjVmOTk2N2UzOWMzNzFmZC9VbnRpdGxlZF9kZXNpZ24ucG5n.webp)

"I wake up every morning grateful for the life I chose, and have found peace and relief.
"My wife and I do not want a life shaped by image, press, or manipulation. All we want peace, privacy and happiness for us and our future family."

Here's a full rundown on the family drama.
Timeline of the Beckham family feud
April 2022: Brooklyn and Nicola tie the knot
On 9 April 2022, Brooklyn and Nicola got married in a lavish ceremony in front of 500 guests at her family's estate in Palm Beach, Florida, two years after getting engaged.
Aug 2022: The first reports of a feud between Nicola and Victoria Beckham
Just months after the wedding, media sources were starting to report on a 'full-on cold war' between Nicola and her new mum-in-law.
According to Page Six, 'the build-up to the wedding was horrendous' and they 'can’t stand each other and don’t talk'.
Reports also claimed much of the feud came from Nicola's decision to wear a Valentino wedding dress instead of a piece designed by Victoria's fashion house, but they appeared to quash these rumours.
March 2023: The Beckhams play happy families
In March 2023, the Beckhams seemed to be happier than ever and were posing for photos at Victoria's Paris fashion show.
April 2025: The family rift resurfaces
Two years on, it was reported that Brooklyn and Nicola had snubbed David's 50th birthday party at Cipriani Downtown Miami.
And then, just days later, TMZ claimed that Brooklyn and brother Romeo weren't speaking due to a fallout over Romeo's girlfriend, Kim Turnbull, who had a 'romantic connection' with Brooklyn 'several years ago'.
Cruz later insisted that Brooklyn and Kim had never actually dated, and in May of 2025, Brooklyn and Nicola were nowhere to be seen as the birthday celebrations for David continued.
July 2025: Mass unfollowing on social media
In July 2025, Brooklyn and Nicola unfollowed Romeo and Cruz and vice versa.
August 2025: David and Victoria miss vow renewals
The following month, David and Victoria are reported not to have attended the Peltz-Beckham vow renewals.
And by December that year, it was reported that Brooklyn no longer followed his parents, and they no longer followed him, and the youngest brother was quick to set the record straight.
Dec 2025: Cruz speaks out
Cruz wrote on his Instagram Stories about the claims that he and his family had unfollowed Brooklyn: "NOT TRUE. My mum and dad would never unfollow their son … Let's get the facts right. They woke up blocked … as did I."
Jan 2026: Brooklyn takes legal action
In January 2026, it was claimed that Brooklyn sent a legal letter to his parents, insisting they only contact him via his lawyer; a rule which Victoria is believed to have broken when she 'liked' an Instagram post he made about a roast chicken.
Jan 2026: Brooklyn breaks silence on family feud
In a shock statement posted on his Instagram Stories on 19 January, Brooklyn made some bombshell claims about his family, which included how his parents have tried to 'ruin' his relationship with Nicola, have always 'controlled' his life, and how 'Brand Beckham' comes first before anything else.
March 2026: David reaches out to Brooklyn
David shared a post to celebrate Brooklyn’s birthday, writing: "27 Today. Happy Birthday Bust. We love you."
He shared an old photo of Brooklyn as a child and tagged Victoria, but was unable to tag Brooklyn since his son has blocked him.
The post was met with stony silence from Brooklyn.
June 2026: Harper turns up at Brooklyn’s door
Harper, Brooklyn’s 14-year-old sister and the Beckhams’ youngest child, was photographed outside Brooklyn’s door hand-delivering a letter. Brooklyn and Nicola were believed to be in New York at the time.
A rep for the Peltz-Beckhams savagely responded: "That photographers were in place as the letter was hand-delivered says it all - this was choreographed for the cameras."
Meanwhile, Brooklyn releases a DoorDash World Cup ad clearly taking a swipe at his family. He says in the commercial: “You’re probably wondering why I’m watching the FIFA World Cup 2026 from home. It’s a long story."

summary: Brooklyn Beckham has covered up his "mama's boy" tattoo dedicated to his mother, Victoria, replacing it with a floral bouquet from his wedding. This follows an ongoing family feud in which Brooklyn cut ties with his parents and siblings, claiming he was controlled by his family for most of his life. While some family-related tattoos like his anchor tribute to David have faded or received cover-ups, other sibling-related tattoos remain visible for now.
key_points: Brooklyn Beckham covered his left pectoral "mama's boy" mother tribute tattoo with a floral bouquet from his 2022 wedding.
His anchor tattoo dedicated to his father, David, has also faded and undergone small cover-ups.
Brooklyn previously issued a statement claiming he cut ties with his family because they controlled him and tried to ruin his relationship with Nicola Peltz.
Despite distancing himself from his parents and siblings, some of his tattoos referencing his siblings have not yet been covered up.

title: TV tonight: David Mitchell’s crime-solving Ludwig returns
author: Phil Harrison; Hollie Richardson; Priya Elan; Simon Wardell; Jack Seale
content:
Ludwig
9pm, BBC One
Is there a danger that, with John “Ludwig” Taylor’s true identity revealed, this cosy-crime drama will lose intrigue in its second series? Jeopardy is just about maintained: John is now a police employee but he’s still investigating his brother’s fate, while solving a case a week in his bumbling style. But chief constable Ziegler is on his case – he knows something’s up, he’s just not sure what. Undemanding fun, enlivened by Mitchell’s lead and Anna Maxwell Martin’s Lucy. Phil Harrison
Dragons’ Den
8pm, BBC One
A big first for the show in its 23rd season: with guest judges Susie Ma and Jenna Meek onboard, there are more female dragons than male. Pitches kick off with Kimberly and her eco-conscious haircare range Selkie, before mother and son Shashi and Sanjay fill the den with Spice Kitchen aromas. Hollie Richardson
The Yorkshire Vet
8pm, Channel 5
Reality show featuring James Herriot’s former trainee Peter, his vet pals and a god-like voiceover from All Creatures Great and Small’s Christopher Timothy. Your enjoyment of the show depends on how much you like watching the surgical treatment of a recently pregnant cow with a prolapse. Priya Elan
![Kate Lister and David Olusoga in A House Through Time.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/1517be0594b734c78eef1e947937506c662369b6/0_0_4100_2716/master/4100.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
A House Through Time
9pm, BBC Two
Back to Edinburgh where David Olusoga is busy bringing more dusty census records to life. We’ve reached the Victorian era in the house on Calton Hill and the residential turnover is brisk. There’s Thomas Mains, a struggling shoe-maker; Thomas Glen, a renowned bagpiper; and, most intriguingly, Catherine Johnston, a brothel keeper. PH
Better Date Than Never
9pm, BBC Three
“Better late than never! Who would have thought?” This dating show is a cheerful treat, following daters who range in age, gender and identity but who have left it late to get into the dating game. This time it’s the turn of Charles, who is trying speed-dating, and Kento, who is excited about a second meeting. PH
Possession
9pm, Sky Atlantic
Karla Crome’s rich, intelligent thriller about the echoing injustices of slavery comes to a mesmeric conclusion, which begins with British-Jamaican lawyer Claudia (Gugu Mbatha-Raw) trapped beneath the floorboards of a house that thrums with past pain. Violent confrontations, in the present day and the 18th century, resolve the narrative in stunning fashion. Jack Seale
Film choice
Novak Djokovic: The Wolf in Winter, Thursday, Prime Video
![Novak Djokovic: The Wolf in Winter.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/bb00f92d772974e298ae2fc8eff8622644593971/0_0_1069_920/master/1069.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
“He’s soft and gentle … but he’s also angry.” Jelena Djokovic’s assessment of her husband is the knotty thread that runs through Jason Hehir’s documentary about a giant of tennis who has yet to be forgiven for surpassing the achievements of crowd favourites Rafael Nadal and Roger Federer. His intensity and stubbornness (a Serbian national trait, we’re told) hasn’t endeared him to the public but, as we go behind the scenes at the 2025 Australian Open and meet an honest, engaging family man with a long history of tough choices, this film could go some way to changing minds. Simon Wardell
summary: Tonight's television highlights include the return of the cosy-crime drama Ludwig on BBC One and a historic lineup featuring more female than male dragons on Dragons' Den. Other notable broadcasts feature historical deep dives on A House Through Time, heartwarming dating stories on Better Date Than Never, and the thrilling conclusion of Possession on Sky Atlantic. Additionally, a documentary exploring the life and career of tennis star Novak Djokovic arrives on Prime Video.
key_points: Ludwig returns for a second series on BBC One, following John Taylor as he continues investigating his brother's fate while solving weekly cases.
Dragons' Den features a first for its 23rd season with more female dragons than male, alongside guest judges Susie Ma and Jenna Meek.
A House Through Time on BBC Two explores Victorian-era Edinburgh residents, including a struggling shoemaker, a bagpiper, and a brothel keeper.
Possession on Sky Atlantic reaches its mesmeric conclusion featuring lawyer Claudia trapped beneath floorboards in a thriller about the injustices of slavery.
A documentary titled Novak Djokovic: The Wolf in Winter examines the tennis star's intensity, public perception, and behind-the-scenes footage from the 2025 Australian Open.

title: Hitchin fruit farm defends Titanic-themed ride after backlash
author: Danny Fullbrook; Nicola Haseler
content:
![An outdoor hydraulic slide designed to look like Titanic. It has a red and blue exterior with a large sign that reads "Titanic".](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/a22b/live/637fbb80-9bd9-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
The ride has received criticism online that it was "disrespectful" to the victims of the 1912 disaster
- Published
The owners of a Titanic-themed ride have defended it after criticism it disrespected those who died in the 1912 disaster.
More than 1,500 people drowned when the ship struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic while on its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York.
The Titanic ride at Graveley Fruit Farm near Hitchin, Hertfordshire, sees the replica ship lift at one end to slide customers downwards, resembling the sinking of the ocean liner.
Manager Will Campbell-Gray said: "We're keeping the memory of Titanic alive and we're not making fun of the dead at all."
He added the ride was renamed The Big Tipper last year after complaints were made online, but the original name was restored after his wife received threats demanding it was changed back.
The Titanic was 269m (882ft) long, 28m (91ft) wide and more than 53m (173ft) tall, and took about three years to build.
Its construction cost Â£1.5m, which is about Â£170m in today's money.
![A ride designed to look like the Titanic. The back of the ride is open and it is painted red and blue. There is bunting above the ride and it is positioned in a field. The photograph is taken on a cloudy day.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/5b85/live/be85bd00-9bce-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
The farm's owners estimate that about 500 people use the ride every day
The ride has received comments on social media calling it "disrespectful" and "odd".
Campbell-Gray highlighted the educational value of the ride, believing it has encouraged children to learn about the history of the ship.
"We've had autistic children who are obsessed with Titanic... they love coming here and going on it because they know all the facts and all the figures," he said.
The ride was constructed last year using repurposed farm materials, including strawberry polytunnel hoops and an old tipper lorry trailer.
He said: "It never even crossed our minds that there would be any backlash."
![A man in a green polo shirt is stood in a field with grey clouds above. He is smiling and looking directly at the camera. He has blond hair.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/3f06/live/e03209e0-9bce-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Will Campbell-Gray said the ride was educational
After receiving complaints last year, the farm had new signs made to rename the ride The Big Tipper, but Campbell-Gray said this caused a "far greater" backlash.
He said: "My wife, who does the social media, got threats... death threats saying that we should change it back.
"So we actually thought long and hard and thought, actually, we're not making fun of the dead or anything.
"Actually it's a nice thing to be a memory of the Titanic and keep the Titanic memory alive."

summary: The owners of Graveley Fruit Farm in Hitchin have defended their Titanic-themed slide after facing online criticism for being disrespectful to victims of the 1912 disaster. Manager Will Campbell-Gray stated that the ride aims to keep the memory of the ship alive and provides educational value, particularly for children interested in its history. The ride was temporarily renamed The Big Tipper following initial complaints, but the original name was restored after the manager's wife received threats demanding the change.
key_points: A Titanic-themed slide at Graveley Fruit Farm lifts at one end to resemble the sinking ship.
The ride faced online backlash and accusations of being disrespectful to 1912 disaster victims.
Manager Will Campbell-Gray defended the attraction, noting its educational value and popularity with children.
The ride was briefly renamed The Big Tipper before reverting to the original name due to threats made against the manager's wife.
The attraction was constructed last year using repurposed farm materials, with an estimated 500 daily users.

title: Man says childhood was 'taken from me' through fake illnesses
author: John Danks; Julia Gregory
content:
![Matthew Johnson is wearing a black T-shirt and is sitting in a chair looking towards an interviewer out of shot.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/390a/live/bb113410-9bec-11f1-aed9-776866bfb986.jpg)
Matthew Johnson said he has processed what happened in his childhood
- Published
A man whose mother falsely claimed he was suffering from serious illnesses as a young boy says part of his childhood was stolen from him.
Lisa Hayden-Johnson from Brixham won public sympathy for her fight for Matthew Johnson's medical care after claiming he was unable to walk, eat or breathe without assistance - she was jailed in 2010 for three years and three months for putting him through unnecessary treatment.
She has now participated in a Channel 4 documentary, as has her son, his sister Laura, doctors from Torbay and police who investigated.
Now 25, Johnson said: "I do think that my childhood was taken from me and that's something that you can't go back to, so it is difficult to process."
![The family are posing besides some stairs. Chris has a white shirt with blue stripes, Matthew has a red top and has a feeding tube and a badge reading Children of Courage, Laura is wearing a brown top and blue denim skirt and Lisa has a pale blue, yellow and brown striped top.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/800/cpsprodpb/b245/live/1ae2a9e0-9bee-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Chris, Matthew, Laura and Lisa at a Children of Courage event
He told the BBC: "You can't really fathom it, it's a really difficult thing to explain. It's such an extraordinary situation.
"I think it definitely impacted me, it's such a key stage of development."
He was born prematurely and fed with a breathing tube before making a full recovery, but his mother insisted he was still unwell for the next six years until a doctor raised the alarm.
She received gifts from charities and took her son to collect an award at Downing Street where they met the then prime minister Tony Blair, and Matthew was also introduced to Camilla, Duchess of Cornwall.
Johnson said his mother had a condition known as fabrication induced illness by proxy.
![Matthew is a young boy and is wearing a blue shirt and shorts. He has a feeding tube which stretches across his face between his nose and mouth.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/eed3/live/b0231680-9bed-11f1-ba30-ddd78081057f.jpg)
Matthew Johnson had a feeding tube as a young boy
He said: "It feels that so many things were declared wrong with me, it was hard to identify with one of them."
He moved away from Devon when he was eight and is now settled in Chesterfield.
He told the BBC he did not remember feeling unwell but had "quite of lot of medication" and even underwent surgery.
He said his mother said he had difficulty breathing, and added: "There were times she said I was damaged by sunlight and had to wear special glasses and when I needed mobility support, whether a stroller a walker or a wheelchair".
'Contradictory'
He said the illnesses he was said to have "seemed contradictory".
"It felt like a trail of different ones, there wasn't anything that seemed permanent."
He said participating in the documentary Love You To Death which also features medics from NHS Torbay, social workers and Devon police helped as he "gained a lot of useful information that I didn't actually know".
Johnson said hearing his mother's comments on the documentary confirmed he had made the correct decision to cut ties with her.
He has not been in touch with her for two years and said it "puts it to rest that I've made the right decision for me and my future".
'I've looked ahead'
He said as he grew up relatives agonised about when to tell him what had happened.
"They didn't want to tell me too early to take me away from the normal life that I was living, but also they didn't want to tell me at a point where I wouldn't fully understand."
He said he processed what happened to him "from things that I had read, from things that people had told me."
Johnson added: "I've just got on with what I've been doing.
"I've looked ahead and didn't want to seek the past because it's not a place that I want to visit.
"So I've always just cracked on with what I want to do for the future."
The documentary Love You to Death is produced by Hugo Pettitt will air on Channel 4 on Wednesday.
Follow BBC Devon on X, external, Facebook, external and Instagram, external. Send your story ideas to spotlight@bbc.co.uk, external.
summary: Matthew Johnson states that part of his childhood was stolen after his mother, Lisa Hayden-Johnson, falsely claimed he suffered from serious illnesses and subjected him to unnecessary medical treatments. His mother was jailed for three years and three months in 2010. Now 25, Johnson has cut ties with her for two years and has participated in a Channel 4 documentary titled Love You To Death to help process his past.
key_points: Lisa Hayden-Johnson falsely claimed her son Matthew could not walk, eat, or breathe without assistance and subjected him to unnecessary treatments.
She was jailed in 2010 for three years and three months for putting him through unnecessary medical procedures.
Matthew Johnson, now 25, stated that his childhood was taken from him by his mother's fabrication induced illness by proxy.
Johnson has not been in touch with his mother for two years and participated in the Channel 4 documentary Love You To Death.
The documentary also features medical professionals, social workers, and police who investigated the case.

title: Sandra Bullock shares she grieved late partner for 'four years' before he died
author: Danni Scott
content:
![](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/comp-1787166935.png?w=646) 
Sandra Bullock has spoken about her late partner, Bryan Randall, for the first time, following his death at the age of 57 in August 2023.
The American actress, 62, confirmed the tragic news with ‘great sadness’ in a statement at the time but has not spoken publicly about the loss in depth.
Bryan died three years after being diagnosed with ALS, a motor neuron disease that causes increased paralysis.
The couple, who had been together for eight years, did not reveal his illness as she has now revealed he had asked her ‘not to share’.
‘I know why he asked me not to,’ she said on the Smartless podcast but admitted that had ‘isolated her in the process’.
Around half of ALS patients are given a three-year prognosis, although some live for far longer, but Sandra said she was ‘grieving Bryan four years before he passed.’
![FILE - AUGUST 07: Sandra Bullock's longtime partner, photographer Bryan Randall, has died at 57 after a battle with ALS. NEW YORK, NY - JUNE 05: Sandra Bullock and Bryan Randall are seen at 'Oceans 8' World Premiere on June 5, 2018 in New York City. (Photo by Jackson Lee/GC Images)](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_166894035-38f2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
‘There was something that had shifted’ she said. ‘My person left a lot earlier than the body left. I don’t think I ever dealt with that until after he passed, because you’re just on this treadmill.’
‘And plus the entire world was locked in with a pandemic. It was literally like the final diagnosis, even though he was ill for half of our relationship.’
She explained that the diagnosis came at almost the same time as ‘the cloak of the pandemic’, which saw everyone shut inside to prevent Covid’s spread.
‘I have a child with severe asthma, I was panicking,’ the Practical Magic star recalled. ‘I had two young kids, that were navigating it, especially a little girl who saw him as a father figure…
‘I wasn’t allowed to tell anybody. My sister was the only one who knew for a while. It’s a huge weight.’
Eventually she did tell her close friend Jennifer Aniston, as well as Smartless host Jason Bateman’s wife Amanda Anaka.
![Sandra Bullock claims she was advised not to 'like' Jennifer Aniston](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_261916047-7e74.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=528) 
In January 2024, Sandra was seen scattering his ashes in the Bahamas to mark his final resting spot.
An insider said at the time that, after the couple first met in 2015, they exchanged their informal ‘vows’ there in 2017 and frequently took family holidays there.
Her sister, Gesine Bullock-Prado had previously confirmed he was also scattered in Wyoming on the banks of Snake River, in a video on Instagram.
On the day that would have been his 58th birthday, she posted: ‘Happy birthday, Bry. Sandy brought you to the river, just as she promised.’

Pictures presentation at The Dolby Colosseum at Caesars Palace during CinemaCon, the official convention of Cinema United, on April 14, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. Shortly after her partner’s death, Sandra was reported to be ‘grateful’ for the support she had received and felt ‘happy’ that people had chosen to donate to ALS charities.
