title: Hayden Panettiere latest: DEA joins investigation into Heroes star’s death
author: Shahana Yasmin; Caitlin Hornik
content:
Hayden Panettiere, who became a household name as a teenager for her role in Heroes and later starred in Nashville and multiple Scream films, has died at age 36.
Panettiere was pronounced dead at a South Carolina apartment Sunday, August 16. A cause of death has not been revealed, but an autopsy showed no signs of trauma. Toxicology reports are pending and could take up to 12 weeks, according to the Greenville County Coroner’s Office.
A newly released incident report states that the 911 call was made by Brian Hickerson, 37, who is referred to as Panettiere’s boyfriend. He reportedly turned over a “bag of medication” belonging to Panettiere to the police, but the contents of that bag has so far been redacted. His brother Zach Hickerson was also present on the scene. The Independent has approached police for further information.
Now, police have reportedly begun probing whether there could be criminal conduct behind her death. Officers with the Greenville Police Department were seen outside of a Hickerson family home Wednesday morning in photos first obtained by Page Six. The US Drug Enforcement Administration joined the investigation into Panettiere’s death on Wednesday, according to a person familiar with the case who spoke to the New York Times.
Among her most memorable roles were Sheryl Yoast in the 2000 Denzel Washington-led film Remember the Titans, high school cheerleader Claire Bennet on NBC’s sci-fi drama Heroes (2006-2010), and aspiring country singer Juliette Barnes on the hit TV series Nashville (2012-2018).
Her New York Times bestselling memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning, was published in May this year, in which she looked back at her childhood in Hollywood and her experiences with addiction, postpartum depression, abusive relationships, and the loss of custody of her daughter, Kaya, whom she shares with former heavyweight boxer Wladimir Klitschko.
Hayden Panettiere dead: Heroes and Nashville star dies aged 36
Hayden Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes, Nashville, and the Scream franchise, has died aged 36.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden,” Panettiere’s father, Skip said in a statement to ABC News. “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”
No cause of death was announced.
![Hayden Panettiere attends Jony And Marc's (RED) Auction at Sotheby's in New York](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/17/04/2026-08-17T031938Z_1937106696_RC230NATJBN1_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-HAYDEN-PANETTIERE.JPG)
Wladimir Klitschko breaks silence over ex-fiancée's death
In an Instagram post, Wladimir Klitschko wrote: “Our family is going through a time of profound shock and grief.
“The announcement of Hayden’s tragic death saddens me deeply. She left this world far too soon. Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya.
“She built an incredible career through immense talent, while also facing the darker sides of a very demanding industry. Nothing will erase the times we shared or the place she had in our lives.
“To our daughter Kaya, I will always speak of her mother with respect and make sure she remembers the person she was.
“I extend my deepest condolences to Hayden’s parents, her friends, and her fans, who are also grieving today. Young and talented people like Hayden should not leave this world so soon.
“I ask everyone to please respect our family’s feelings and privacy during this incredibly difficult time. For now, this is all I wish to say.
“Thank you to everyone who is supporting my family and expressing their sincere condolences.
“Rest easy, Hayden. May you find eternal peace. #WeLoveYouHayden”
Hayden Panettiere’s old injuries left her in severe pain before her death
Hayden Panettiere was still dealing with severe physical pain in the months before her death, more than two decades after an on-set accident while filming Racing Stripes.
While filming the 2005 movie at 14, Panettiere was thrown from a zebra and suffered a concussion, whiplash, and injuries to her neck. In her memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning, she wrote: “I kept my mouth shut and endured the pain in my back and neck. Over 20 years later, these injuries still bother me.”
Earlier this year, she described waking up with “nothing but pins and needles from my waist down” and being unable to bend her toes or lift her foot. “I was sitting there going, ‘Oh, my gosh, am I going to be paralysed for the rest of my life?’” she told Women’s Health.
Her friend and hairstylist Erick Orellana later told Page Six that the actor “suffered earlier this year with her back”, adding: “At one point, it was even hard for her to move her legs.”
Hayden Panettiere had planned to spend 37th birthday with daughter Kaya
Hayden Panettiere had been planning to spend the week of her 37th birthday with her 11-year-old daughter Kaya in Germany.
“She was planning on spending the week of her birthday visiting her daughter in Germany,” a source close to the actor told Page Six. “She was so excited to see her and was telling everyone how much she was looking forward to spending time with her.”
Panettiere would have turned 37 on 21 August, five days after her death.
Her hairstylist and close friend Erick Orellana had previously told Page Six that Panettiere had been “talking about how she wanted to take a vacation, and that she wanted to go and see her daughter”.
Panettiere shared Kaya with former fiancé Wladimir Klitschko. Although Klitschko was granted custody in 2018 while Panettiere sought treatment for addiction and postpartum depression, she continued to speak about her close relationship with her daughter.
Hayden Panettiere’s Heroes father says she was ‘hunted’ by paparazzi as a teenager
Heroes star Jack Coleman has said he is “heartbroken” at the news of Hayden Panettiere’s death, and called out the predatory paparazzi he said “hunted” her.
Coleman, who played Claire Bennet’s father Noah on the NBC series, said Panettiere introduced herself by shouting “daddy” and embracing him when they first met for the pilot 20 years ago. She later called him “daddio”, while he nicknamed her “Haydini” because “she was a magician”.
He recalled the “prodigious talent” of Panettiere, who was 16 when Heroes premiered, and remembered how she was able to cry at the same time during an early scene take after take. “It’s not technique,” she told him. “I feel it and the tears just happen to come at that moment.”
“She was hunted. Everywhere she went, there were photographers with 300 millimeter lenses,” he wrote. “Once, when she came to our house, paparazzi hid in the bushes behind our yard and drove onto neighbours’ lawns. They were predatory. No one, especially a teenager, should be targeted that way.”
“She was blessed and cursed,” Coleman wrote. “She was vulnerable. She felt everything.” He ended by writing: “I only wish you had been given that same protection.”
Hayden Panettiere's TV history
After getting her start on the ABC soap opera One Life to Live, Hayden Panettiere went on to act in a number of TV shows, eventually starring in hit shows Heroes and Nashville. Below is a list of TV shows she appeared on, according to her IMDb page:
- Aliens in the Family
- Unhappily Ever After
- One Life to Live
- Too Rich: The Secret Life of Doris Duke
- Touched by an Angel
- Guiding Light
- Ally McBeal
- Fillmore!
- Law & Order: Special Victims Unit
- Malcolm in the Middle
- Commander in Chief
- Skater Boys
- Robot Chicken
- Heroes
- American Dad!
- Heroes Reborn
- Nashville
Christy Carlson Romano says ‘early fame is like CTE’ after Hayden Panettiere’s death
Even Stevens star Christy Carlson Romano has called for greater protections for child actors following Hayden Panettiere’s death.
“Early fame is like CTE. Not as a diagnosis. As a way of thinking about repeated impact,” Romano wrote in an essay for Elle, comparing the effects of childhood fame to chronic traumatic encephalopathy, a degenerative brain disease caused by repeated head injuries.
“Is it any wonder so many of us struggle with addiction? The industry gives us the wound and then acts surprised when we reach for something to treat it,” she wrote.
Romano, who also began working as a child actor, said young performers face “stress, scrutiny, rejection, adult pressure, and the collapse of privacy” before they are equipped to deal with them. “We need to stop calling the truth bitterness,” she wrote.
Neighbour says she repeatedly called police over Hayden Panettiere’s on-and-off boyfriend
A former neighbour of Hayden Panettiere has described repeated disturbances involving her on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson, saying she called 911 “at least half a dozen times”.
Mia Terrazzas told Inside Edition that she noticed signs of domestic violence and claimed Panettiere appeared frightened during one incident. “I saw her leaving on a gurney. Brian was right next to her, and I asked her if she was okay” she said.
Terrazzas claimed it “looked to me that she had suffered some type of trauma that looked to be battering”.
She also alleged that homeowners’ association notices were posted warning residents to call 911 if Hickerson was seen at the property, although she said they were removed about a week later.
Panettiere detailed years of physical abuse by Hickerson in her memoir, writing that he had tried to smash her head into a wall and “bust up her face so badly I don’t leave the house for weeks”.
Hickerson pleaded no contest in April 2021 to two felony counts of injuring a spouse or girlfriend and was sentenced to 45 days in county jail, four years’ probation, 52 domestic-violence classes and a five-year protective order. He ultimately served 13 days in jail.
Brian Hickerson dealt legal blow in Panettiere case days before star's death
Brian Hickerson, Panettiere’s on-off boyfriend, was denied a request to expunge and downgrade his previous felony charges to misdemeanors days before the Heroes star’s death.
The charges stemmed from several alleged incidents involving Panettiere between May 2019 and January 2020.
Following his July 2020 arrest, Hickerson pleaded no contest to two felony counts of injuring a spouse or girlfriend. He was hit with an eight-count criminal indictment in April 2021.
Hickerson was sentenced to 45 days in jail in 2021, along with four years of probation, 52 mandatory domestic violence classes, and a five-year restraining order.
Page Six reported that Hickerson’s request was denied during an August 13 court hearing, despite arguing that the terms of his probation had been met. Hickerson previously made the same request in July 2025, which was also denied.
Hickerson was with Panettiere at the time of her death.
DEA joins investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s death
The US Drug Enforcement Administration has joined the investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s death, according to a person familiar with the case who spoke to the New York Times.
Panettiere, 36, was found in cardiac arrest at an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina, on Sunday and could not be revived.
A person with knowledge of the investigation told the Times that an apparent drug overdose led to the cardiac arrest, although her official cause of death has not been determined.
The DEA’s involvement comes after police found Panettiere’s former boyfriend Brian Hickerson at the apartment and he showed officers a bag containing medication she had been taking. The details of those medications were redacted from the police report.
Police have said there were no signs of foul play, while toxicology results are still pending.
summary: Actor Hayden Panettiere has died at age 36 at a South Carolina apartment, prompting an ongoing investigation that now involves the US Drug Enforcement Administration and local police. While an autopsy showed no immediate signs of trauma, toxicology reports are pending and an apparent drug overdose is suspected. Her on-and-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, made the 911 call and handed police a bag of medication belonging to Panettiere.
key_points: Hayden Panettiere passed away at the age of 36 in a South Carolina apartment on Sunday, August 16.
An autopsy revealed no physical signs of trauma, but official toxicology results could take up to 12 weeks.
The US Drug Enforcement Administration joined the police investigation into her death.
Brian Hickerson, her on-off boyfriend, made the 911 call and provided police with a bag of Panettiere's medication.

title: Sheffield man speaks out on Devon mum who faked childhood illness
author: Julia Bryson
content:
![A family of a man, woman and two children, a young girl and boy. The boy is wearing a red top and has a tube which goes into his nose. Chris, Matthew, Laura and Lisa Hayden-Johnson](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/720/cpsprodpb/11f8/live/fce3df00-9bc9-11f1-98c6-93bfcdb08681.jpg)
Matthew Johnson said watching the documentary solidified his decision not to speak to his mother
- Published
As a child, Matthew Johnson was known as "Britain's sickest boy" - but in reality, his illness was just a fantasy made up by his mother to gain publicity and financial rewards.
For six-and-a-half years, Lisa Hayden-Johnson claimed Matthew had a long list of illnesses including diabetes, food allergies, cerebral palsy and cystic fibrosis, but years later it emerged she had made it all up.
Hayden-Johnson, from Torbay, Devon, was jailed and Matthew went into foster care and started a new life in Sheffield.
Both were interviewed for a Channel 4 documentary called Love You To Death but after hearing his mother speak, Matthew said he had "mixed emotions" and it reinforced his decision not to speak to her.
Speaking to the BBC about how it felt to hear his mother's point of view, he said: "It was a lot of disappointment but I think also frustration as almost two decades on, there is still a lack of accountability from her side.
"When I could see, even after two decades... she still holds the same story and believes that she did the best by me... that obviously isn't right."
Hayden-Johnson was 35 when she was jailed for three years and three months by a judge at Exeter Crown Court in 2010.
The court heard her lies began when Matthew was born prematurely in 2001 and given a tube for feeding.
He recovered but his mother insisted that this was not the case.
![A man with dark brown hair wearing a blue shift and dark jumper.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/3090/live/31c21ed0-9bd9-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Matthew Johnson said his mother "still holds the same story" after two decades
Hayden-Johnson lied about her son's health for years, claiming he had symptoms despite doctors being unable to find any.
She also told doctors the child had diabetes and spiked his urine samples with glucose in order to fool tests.
Doctors, friends, family and even the boy's father believed the child was unable to eat or swallow food.
Her actions led to Matthew being operated on and being fed through a tube in his stomach.
She introduced him in a wheelchair to the then Duchess of Cornwall, now Queen Camilla, appeared on television and amassed Â£130,000 in benefits after claiming Â£20,000 a year in disability living allowance.
She was given gifts from children's charities including a new car, a cruise in Tenerife, and also free X-Factor tickets.
It wasn't until 2007 that a paediatrician became suspicious that Matthew's health problems had gone on for so long without a clear diagnosis.
Hayden-Johnson was eventually arrested in October 2007 and jailed three years later.
![A mother and child in a church, the child is a young boy who has a tube in his nose and a red badge which reads 'Women's Own Children of Courage'](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1920/cpsprodpb/173d/live/4fba20d0-9bda-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Matthew said he wants to focus on his life now and leave the past behind
Matthew said thinking back to the time his mother's lies unravelled was like a "fever dream".
"I was taken into foster care. I was looked after by a few different people, taken away from my dad and my sister, the family pets. It was quite difficult," he said.
"But as I look back, it was something that happened quite quickly and I was able to draw a fresh slate when I moved to Sheffield and that's how I've sort of managed to move on from it.
"I always like to say that my life mainly started when I was in Sheffield and I can just make the most of that part and leave the other part behind."
![A woman with auburn chin-length hair in a green top and black suit jacket, wearing a silver crucifix.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/3400/live/29b87900-9bd9-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Hayden-Johnson, from Torbay, Devon, said she acted in her son's best interests
He credits his family and friends for helping him through his ordeal.
"My sister Laura has been really supportive throughout the whole process. We've always been side by side."
Matthew's father was cleared of any involvement as he was also duped by Hayden-Johnson.
"My dad's always looked after me," Matthew said.
"His life got turned upside down at the same time, so I really appreciate everything he's done for me throughout the years.
"Also, I think you kind of just have to carry yourself through it because there's only really you that can decide what mindset you choose to have on it.
"I think that's the most important part. It's the decision to not dwell and the decision to look forward rather than in the past."
Love You To Death will be broadcast on Channel 4 at 21:00 BST.
If you've been affected by the issues in this story, help and support is available via BBC Action Line
summary: Matthew Johnson, once known as "Britain's sickest boy," has spoken out after his mother, Lisa Hayden-Johnson, faked numerous illnesses for years to gain publicity, gifts, and financial rewards. Hayden-Johnson was jailed in 2010 after a paediatrician grew suspicious, leading to Matthew being placed in foster care and starting a new life in Sheffield. Following a recent documentary featuring both of them, Matthew expressed disappointment over his mother's continued lack of accountability and reinforced his decision to cut ties with her.
key_points: Lisa Hayden-Johnson falsely claimed for over six years that her son Matthew suffered from severe illnesses like cystic fibrosis and cerebral palsy.
Her actions resulted in unnecessary medical procedures for Matthew, £130,000 in fraudulent benefits, and charity gifts before she was jailed in 2010.
Matthew was taken into foster care in 2007 before eventually starting a new life in Sheffield.
After watching a Channel 4 documentary featuring his mother, Matthew stated she still lacks accountability and maintains she did the best for him.

title: Supergirl actor announces shock retirement after becoming 'fed up'
author: Brooke Ivey Johnson
content:
![David Krumholtz](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804371-fdb4-e1787130821269.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Actor David Krumholtz has revealed he is taking an indefinite break from acting after becoming ‘frustrated’ and ‘fed up’ with Hollywood.
The 48-year-old, whose career has spanned more than three decades, surprised fans when he announced he had ‘kinda sorta’ put his acting career on hold in a candid Threads post on Tuesday.
Krumholtz, who played physicist Isidor Rabi in Christopher Nolan’s Oscar-winning Oppenheimer and is also well known for The Santa Clause franchise as well as a recent role in Supergirl, admitted he had been terrified of making the decision for years.
But after finally taking the plunge, he said he was hit with an unexpected sense of relief.
‘I kinda sorta put my acting career on hold the other day,’ he wrote in the now-deleted post.
‘There was a time when being competitive and self-involved really served my pursuit. That time has passed.’
![SUPERGIRL, David Krumholtz as Zor-El, 2026. ph: Parisa Taghizadeh / ? Warner Bros. / courtesy Everett Collection](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804374-6255.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Krumholtz explained that he had long worried about what walking away from the industry could mean for him financially.
He said stepping back had ‘been something I’ve been petrified to do for years,’ admitting he feared he would ‘go broke and not be able to handle being out of the game.’
However, those fears seemingly gave way to relief once he made his decision official. ‘A huge wave of relief washed over me when I sent the definitive email,’ he continued.
‘Not sure what I’m going to do for money instead, or how I’m going to do it, but I just removed a humongous burden, one that I truly didn’t fathom the weight of until it was gone.’
![Publicity Film Still from "The Santa Clause" Tim Allen, David Krumholtz ? 1994 Walt Disney Pictures Photo Credit: Attila Dory](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804436-ae6d.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Summing up his feelings towards the profession, he added simply: ‘Frustrated, fed up, fried.’
The original announcement was subsequently deleted, but Krumholtz returned to Threads after being inundated with messages from fans and fellow actors.
He described the ‘love and encouragement’ he had received as ‘overwhelmingly surprising’ and clarified that he had not fallen out of love with acting itself.
Instead, it was the realities of pursuing it professionally that had apparently lost their appeal: ‘Acting professionally is a very different concept than the exercise of acting itself.
‘I’ve enjoyed every single minute of exercising the muscle. I’ve enjoyed the fanfare.’
He reiterated that the competitive mindset which once helped drive his career was no longer something he wanted to embrace.
![Ben Stiller and David Krumholtz](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804375-36ca.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
‘There will always be great joy in the exercise. But for me, the profession has lost its gleam,’ he said.
Despite the dramatic announcement, Krumholtz later stressed that fans should not necessarily consider his departure permanent.
Responding to fellow actor Geoffrey Blake, who told him he was ‘too good to quit’, Krumholtz clarified: ‘Not quitting entirely.’
Instead, he described his decision as ‘taking a bit of a step back and an indefinite break’.
He added that the pressures surrounding his career had left him questioning whether he might have a different purpose outside the industry.
!["Harold & Kumar Escape from Guantanamo Bay" David Krumholtz, Eddie Kaye Thomas ? 2008 New Line Cinema](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804423-d896.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
‘The stress of the moment has me wondering if there’s a higher calling to pursue,’ he wrote.
Actor Garret Dillahunt was also among those to offer his support, telling Krumholtz: ‘This is sad news for me. But I am happy for you. I understand completely.’
Krumholtz replied that his career was not necessarily ‘over,’ but that he wanted to redefine the terms on which he worked.
‘Hoping to find a new, more rewarding passion,’ he said. ‘Me, my product, and I mentality is not working anymore. I want to try to be of service. No crystal ball.’
His decision comes despite Krumholtz remaining busy on screen in recent years.
![David Krumholtz and Macaulay Culkin David Krumholtz and Macaulay Culkin at the reading of 'Spectacle, Part One of the Mark Rosen Chronicles' at the Nantucket Community School during the 10th Annual Nantucket Film Festival on June 17, 2005. Nantucket, Massachusetts Photo ? Matt Baron/BEImages](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804427-1f2b.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
After appearing in Oppenheimer in 2023, he went on to feature in 2025 Bruce Springsteen biopic Springsteen: Deliver Me from Nowhere and appeared in 2026’s Supergirl.
Krumholtz began acting as a child, landing film roles in Life with Mikey and Addams Family Values in 1993 before appearing as Bernard the elf in 1994 festive favourite The Santa Clause.
- 
	![Susanna Reid nearly unrecognisable raving at Ibiza super club](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308762990-3293.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=38px%2C0px%2C1129px%2C635px&resize=646%2C363)
- Hayden Panettiere's 'unexpected' death triggers criminal investigation
- John Cleese asks who Roman Kemp and Lauren Laverne are in toe-curling live TV moment
- Hayden Panettiere's body was 'found by boyfriend Brian Hickerson's brother'
He reprised the role in its 2002 sequel and, decades later, returned to the character for Disney series The Santa Clauses.
![Joseph Gordon-Levitt, David Krumholtz Director: Gil Junger Touchstone USA Scene Still Shakespeare Comedy](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308804364-e229.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
His lengthy film CV also includes Slums of Beverly Hills, 10 Things I Hate About You, Ray, Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle, Superbad and Sausage Party.
On television, he is perhaps best known for starring as mathematician Charlie Eppes in crime drama Numb3rs, which ran for six seasons.
He has also appeared in Freaks and Geeks, ER, The Closer, Monty, Chicago Sons and The Trouble with Normal.
summary: Actor David Krumholtz has announced an indefinite break from acting after more than three decades in the industry, citing frustration with Hollywood's professional demands and competitive nature. Although he initially posted that he was putting his career on hold due to feeling 'fried' and 'fed up,' he later clarified that he is not quitting entirely but stepping back to find a new, more rewarding passion. Krumholtz, known for his roles in Oppenheimer, The Santa Clause, and Supergirl, expressed a strong sense of relief after making the decision.
key_points: David Krumholtz announced an indefinite break from his acting career in a candid Threads post.
The 48-year-old actor stated he became frustrated, fed up, and tired of the competitive nature of the profession.
Despite initial financial fears, Krumholtz felt an immediate wave of relief after sending the definitive email to step back.
He clarified that he has not fallen out of love with acting itself, but rather the realities of pursuing it professionally.
Krumholtz's extensive career includes roles in Oppenheimer, The Santa Clause franchise, Numb3rs, and Supergirl.

title: Prince Harry and Meghan ‘moving back to Britain this month’
author: Nadeem Badshah
content:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are planning to return to live in Britain, six years after leaving for the US, it has been reported.
The couple and their two children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, are expected to relocate later this month to a non-royal residence.
The property is believed to be outside London, and the children are enrolled to start school in September, the Daily Telegraph reported.
King Charles was informed on Sunday that his son and daughter-in-law would return to Britain, according to the Telegraph.
It comes after the Sussexes, who have lived in California since 2020, had a reunion with the king last month at Highgrove in Gloucestershire.
The king is said to welcome the opportunity to see more of his family in a personal capacity but there will be no change in their status as private individuals after relinquishing their official working roles within the royal family.
The Prince and Princess of Wales are said to have also been informed of the decision.
The couple are expected to retain their homes in Montecito, California, and Portugal, where they went on holiday earlier this summer.
The duke and duchess’s security arrangements have not been disclosed.
The long-running issue over their security meant that Prince Harry did not bring Meghan, 45, or their children to events in London last month, as had been originally planned.
Prince Harry, 41, has previously stressed he would not feel safe bringing his family back to the UK without police protection.
In May 2025, after losing a legal challenge over his security in the UK, the Duke of Sussex said: “I can’t see a world in which I would bring my wife and children back to the UK at this point.”
In an interview with the BBC after the ruling, Prince Harry said he “would love a reconciliation” with the royal family.
He said: “There have been so many disagreements between myself and some of my family,” but he had now “forgiven” them.
“I would love reconciliation with my family. There’s no point continuing to fight any more, life is precious.”
Prince Harry added the dispute over his security had “always been the sticking point”.
Asked whether he had asked the king to intervene in the dispute over security, he said: “I never asked him to intervene – I asked him to step out of the way and let the experts do their jobs.”
Last month, the Duke of Sussex and six other co-claimants lost their privacy case against the publishers of the Daily Mail in London. The claimants, who included Doreen Lawrence and Elton John, sued Associated Newspapers Ltd over allegations of unlawful information gathering. Their claims were dismissed in their entirety by Mr Justice Nicklin.
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are reportedly planning to move back to Britain from California this month with their two children. King Charles and the Prince and Princess of Wales were reportedly informed of the decision following a recent family reunion at Highgrove. The couple's return comes despite ongoing disputes regarding their UK security arrangements, and their official working roles within the royal family will remain unchanged.
key_points: Prince Harry and Meghan are reportedly moving back to Britain this month with their children, Archie and Lilibet.
King Charles and the Prince and Princess of Wales were informed of the relocation plan.
The couple plans to live in a non-royal residence outside London and enroll their children in school for September.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are expected to retain their homes in California and Portugal.
Security arrangements for the family have not been disclosed, following previous legal challenges regarding UK police protection.

title: Adam Copeland Reveals Surprising Retirement Plan (AEW News)
author: Michael Hamflett
content:
![Adam Copeland](https://d2thvodm3xyo6j.cloudfront.net/media/2026/02/452a63dde9ec44d9057b3649577dee18.jpg) 
Adam Copeland has said he will retire in All Elite Wrestling.
Speaking to Ariel Helwani, the former multi-time WWE Champion said he had no desire to see out his career with the market leader, instead choosing to stay in his current role in AEW.
He said; “That’s where I want to retire. I know that may disappoint a lot of people, but I love it there. I love the company. I love the attitude. I love the exuberance. I love the drive. I love the excitement I see from the locker room. I don’t want to go anywhere else. I’m good. I did everything I could do there (WWE) and then some. And I think they got everything out of me and then some that they could have.”
'Cope' debuted for All Elite Wrestling at WrestleDream 2023, and (as of writing) has worked almost 50 matches for the company ever since. He's competed for the World Heavyweight Championship, has held the TNT Championship and is currently one half of the AEW World Tag Team Champions alongside former Edge & Christian partner Christian Cage. The pair are set to work a dream match against the Young Bucks at Wembley Stadium when the company presents All In: London on August 30th, which very much supports Copeland's point about still having new things to do. He spent three years with WWE following his remarkable return from injury at the 2020 Royal Rumble, main eventing a WrestleMania along the way before wrapping up his run in August 2023 with a win over a Sheamus on a special edition of SmackDown at the Scotiabank Arena in his hometown of Toronto.
summary: Professional wrestler Adam Copeland has announced that he intends to finish his career in All Elite Wrestling rather than return to WWE. In an interview with Ariel Helwani, Copeland expressed his love for AEW's locker room culture, attitude, and drive. Since debuting for AEW at WrestleDream 2023, he has held multiple championships and is currently a co-holder of the AEW World Tag Team Championship.
key_points: Adam Copeland stated he plans to retire in All Elite Wrestling.
He praised AEW's locker room attitude, exuberance, and drive.
Copeland debuted for AEW in October 2023 and has wrestled nearly 50 matches for the company.
He previously spent three years in WWE following his 2020 return before finishing his run there in August 2023.
He currently holds the AEW World Tag Team Championship alongside Christian Cage.

title: Mutiny review – Jason Statham’s fight-by-numbers action thriller just about stays above water
author: Benjamin Lee
content:
The dog days of August have already seen the trotting out of some usual suspects from a junky Eli Roth horror to a belated nostalgia comedy sequel to a Mike Pence-approved Ronald Reagan drama. This weekend, yet more howls will be heard in cinemas with a lower-tier horror instalment and an even lower-tier girlies on tour comedy being shuffled out. It’s all amounting to a rather rubbishy end to what’s been a pretty remarkable summer (easily the biggest since the pandemic), allowing for Spider-Man supremacy until September slowly returns the industry from the D-list closer to the A.
There can still be low-level popcorn pleasures to be had in August. Last weekend’s throwback dino caper The End of Oak Street was a B-movie made with just the right balance of serious to silly while last year Zach Cregger gifted us Weapons, the rare genre film to end up winning an Oscar. Trophies are unlikely for this weekend’s other medium-sized release Mutiny (if only the Blockbuster Entertainment Awards hadn’t died off at the turn of the 2000s) but if the words “Jason Statham vehicle” possess a safe, soothing quality then there are far worse ways to spend a Saturday night.
The actor occupies a rarefied space in a genre that now mostly exists far away from the big screen, pushed back toward the contemporary equivalent of the DVD bargain bin. Outside of the superhero world or some other more fantastical setting, the action movie has struggled at the box office, at least domestically (it remains easily sellable overseas). Without a generation of younger stars taking on impossible missions, it’s been left to the older guard to kick, shoot and try not to keel over, an ever-decreasing squad which is now led by Gerard Butler and Statham (Liam Neeson’s action movie overkill means they barely get released these days). Both have managed to stay working above the glut of even lower-rent, straight-to-streaming titles and they can still manage to attract a decent-sized audience, usually in January or August, kings of the dumping months.
For his latest Statham has borrowed Jean-François Richet, the French director of Butler’s 2023 hit Plane, a film I found personally disappointing for its unforgivably small amount of actual plane. That film was supposed to be followed by Ship (I kid you not) but reportedly, Butler dropped out just two weeks before production and it was canned. Perhaps the deposit for the ship had already been paid as it’s hard not to see how Mutiny isn’t what that film ultimately morphed into, another by-the-book tale of a hero striking back at crooks, also sharing the same co-writer. If Plane suffered from not enough plane then Mutiny keeps us satisfyingly with ship for almost the entirety as Statham’s ex-cop turned bodyguard cons his away on to a cargo voyage to find out who is behind the murder of his billionaire boss.
Perhaps there’s something slightly more charming about the existence of a sturdy and unpretentious formula-first actioner like Mutiny just because it’s that much less common to see a film like this actually reach the big screen in 2026. It also helps that by this stage Statham knows how to go through the motions but doesn’t seem to sleepwalk through them just yet. His line reading can be stiff and hammy but that only adds to the charm while as an action star he is never less than physically persuasive. Richet is as competent as the film requires, efficiently staging tightly restricted fisticuffs in-between storage containers and throwing in some gloriously gory embellishments (who knew a padlock could be so gruesomely useful?) but it’s all rather plain and workmanlike (as a Statham director, Richet is very much not Guy Ritchie). So very much of Mutiny is just exactly what one expects without any added seasoning, no emotional reaction or character motivation or plot twist bringing us to a place we didn’t expect to be.
Which means that of course, Statham teams up with an attractive blond woman, played by Annabelle Wallis as a single mother turned feisty third mate (her character has a “deadbeat ex and the most wonderful little girl in the world” naturally) and of course they’re also trying to save a container of Thai refugees at the same time for maximum goodness and of course, the big reveal at the end is one that we worked out in the very first scene (although admittedly, I wasn’t as prepared for two small roles for White Lotus season three actors, sadly not including Parker Posey). It feels like something you might have half-seen before and for the meantime, it’s likely to be something you’ll half-see again. The action genre is undoubtedly in need of new tricks but until they come, films like Mutiny offer a modestly entertaining reminder of what the old dogs can still do.
- 
  Mutiny is out in Australian cinemas on 20 August and in the US and UK on 21 August
summary: Jason Statham stars in the new action thriller "Mutiny," directed by Jean-François Richet, playing an ex-cop turned bodyguard who investigates his billionaire boss's murder on a cargo ship. The film relies heavily on a predictable, formulaic plot with standard genre tropes, including fight scenes among storage containers and a familiar twist. Despite lacking originality, the movie delivers modest, workmanlike entertainment typical of a traditional Statham vehicle.
key_points: "Mutiny" stars Jason Statham as an ex-cop turned bodyguard trying to solve the murder of his billionaire boss aboard a cargo ship.
The film was directed by Jean-François Richet, who previously directed Gerard Butler in the film "Plane."
The plot features predictable action-movie tropes, such as a predictable ending twist, an attractive co-star, and a subplot involving refugees.
The movie is scheduled for release in Australian cinemas on August 20, and in the US and UK on August 21.

title: Exclusive: Harry and Meghan plan move back to Britain
author: Victoria Ward
content:
![Prince Harry and Meghan](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498866743_17871632651010_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwWPw2b5__oFarkj5WlWIJuI.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Prince Harry and Meghan](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498866743_17871632651010_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwWPw2b5__oFarkj5WlWIJuI.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are planning to move back to Britain, The Telegraph can reveal.
The family intends to relocate from the US later this month to a private, non-royal residence thought to be outside London.
Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, the couple’s children, are enrolled to start at a British school in September.
There are no current plans for either the Duke or Duchess of Sussex to reprise their official working roles within the Royal family. However, the move raises the prospect that they could do so in the future.
The King was informed of the move on Sunday. It was not discussed when the Sussexes visited him at Highgrove in July, it is understood. He was said to be naturally pleased for the opportunity to see more of his family on a regular basis, both in a private and personal capacity.
However, the King is clear that the Duke and Duchess’s status as non-working royals and private individuals, in keeping with their previously expressed wishes, will remain unchanged.
The Prince and Princess of Wales have also been informed of the move.
![The Duke and Duchess with their children, Lilibet and Archie](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000453992647_17871459552520_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqCu-rHd-sgjqZvaAjQdr_s9luWBnPl6Sn_iGFrIRcxE.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The Duke and Duchess’s security arrangements have not been disclosed, but there has been no announcement of any change. Prince Harry has previously made it clear that he would not feel safe bringing his family back to the UK without police protection, something he has been fighting for for several years.
The British state has so far steadfastly refused to provide him with police support.
The couple will retain their homes in Montecito, California, and Portugal, while the Duchess will continue to run her lifestyle brand As Ever – which sources insist is thriving – from their new base.
Sources suggested that the UK would be their primary home for an extended period, although it had not yet been decided whether to make the move permanent. The locations of the home and school have not been made public for privacy reasons.
The decision comes more than six years after the couple quit royal duties and moved abroad in search of financial independence, agreeing not to use their HRH titles.
In a statement released in 2021, following a 12-month review of their situation, Elizabeth II confirmed that the couple would not “continue with the responsibilities and duties that come with a life of public service”.
She had made it clear that they could not maintain a “half-in, half-out” approach to royal duties while also pursuing commercial opportunities. The Duke and Duchess responded by saying: “We can all live a life of service. Service is universal.”
Prince Harry was stripped of his honorary military titles but has continued to support a handful of charities. The couple believe they have since proved that the “half-in, half-out” model does work.
After moving to the US, the Duke and Duchess made a series of incendiary allegations that shook the Royal family to its core.
They suggested that senior royals were racist by asking questions about the colour of their unborn son’s skin. The Duchess of Sussex also revealed that she had had suicidal thoughts and had struggled with her mental health after joining the Royal family.
![The Duke and Duchess](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000473770726_17871504877150_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqvoXbRQehuJNQprvLCxGprovjVPZKjB48ONGNjYqQH1M.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
She said in a 2019 television interview that British friends had warned her before marrying Prince Harry that the tabloids would destroy her life, and she described the British way of dealing with emotions as “probably really damaging”.
In a 2022 magazine interview, she alleged that she would “never be able to do school pick-up and drop-off” in Britain “without it being a royal photo call”.
While the Duke has started building bridges with his father, his relationship with his brother, Prince William, remains deeply fractured.
The pair are not thought to have spoken for years. Both the Prince and Princess of Wales are said to feel deeply betrayed by the revelations made in the Duke’s memoir, Spare, and in various television interviews.
![The Prince and Princess of Wales with Harry](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/royal-family/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000498851847_17871526761720_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqMG9jYnib85FJIfCc-bQYcSXF5qJfRX82QwtVzSKzjL8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
However, Prince Harry has long made it clear that he misses the UK and is desperate for his children to experience British life and culture.
The move will also enable him to dedicate further time to his charitable organisations.
Invictus 2027 takes place in Birmingham next July, and the Duke fervently hopes that the King will join him to open the event.
![Harry at the Invictus games](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/briefs/2026/08/19/TELEMMGLPICT000494697482_17871505462100_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqaBJSHwufYM_Fh0ArUj1hel5NUcTKNHKqy85KLqtvPLE.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
His relationship with his father has improved in recent months, with the pair chatting regularly on the phone.
When the Duke and Duchess returned to the UK last month, they enjoyed a long-awaited reunion with the King and Queen at Highgrove, the monarch’s Gloucestershire home.
It was a significant moment and marked the first time Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet had seen their grandfather in four years. The meeting was considered a key step on the road to reconciliation.
The Sussexes have already sought to build a base in Europe, buying property in Portugal, at the prestigious Costa Terra resort in Melides, in 2023. The country is popular with US emigrants and offers a so-called golden visa granting EU residency in exchange for an investment of at least €250,000 (£216,000), provided the visa holders stay in the country for seven days a year.
summary: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex are planning to relocate from the United States to a private residence in Britain later this month, with their children enrolled to start at a British school in September. The King and the Prince and Princess of Wales have been informed of the move, though the couple will remain non-working royals. The UK is intended to serve as their primary home for an extended period, while they also retain properties in California and Portugal.
key_points: Prince Harry and Meghan are planning to move back to Britain from the US later this month.
Their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, are enrolled to start at a British school in September.
The King was informed of the move and is pleased to see more of his family, but the couple's status as non-working royals will remain unchanged.
The couple will keep their homes in Montecito and Portugal while using the UK as their primary residence for an extended period.

title: Emma Barnett: Broadcaster reveals she had hysterectomy after making film about endometriosis
author: Paul Glynn; Ian Youngs
content:
![Emma Barnett wearing glasses while filming part of her Fighting Endometriosis documentary](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1536/cpsprodpb/8625/live/15d6ccd0-9bc4-11f1-98c6-93bfcdb08681.jpg)
Barnett said it was "totally surreal" to be in hospital on the night her documentary was broadcast
- Published
BBC presenter Emma Barnett has revealed she had a hysterectomy and surgery for endometriosis days before a documentary she made about the condition was broadcast.
Barnett, 41, returned to Radio 4's Today programme on Wednesday morning, explaining she had been absent in recent weeks because she was in hospital "in a case of life imitating work".
She told listeners: "I made a programme on endometriosis on BBC Two and ended up being in hospital for endometriosis.
"So yes, I've been recuperating, shall we say, from surgery for endometriosis and a hysterectomy to boot. So that's been less fun than the Today programme, but it is lovely to be back."
Barnett's announcement came soon after she published a blog about the "hysterectomy I never wanted to have", external.
The presenter, who has two children, said it was "totally surreal" to be in hospital on the night her documentary was broadcast in June, only well enough to watch the final 10 minutes.
"Some 48 hours before the documentary aired - I had undergone a near-5 hour surgery and somehow found myself lying in bed recovering from extensive endometriosis surgery, a hysterectomy and a gallbladder removal," she wrote.
"Triple threat. Go big or go home. Life imitating art."
She added: "I felt blind-sided and robbed, even though my care had been superb and doctors, utterly brilliant.
"But this was not the road I had envisioned for myself. I had the hysterectomy I never wanted to have."
Endometriosis is where cells similar to those in the lining of the womb grow in other parts of the body, resulting in what Barnett has described as "bone-grinding, life-altering pain". It affects one in 10 women and there is no known cure.
A hysterectomy is a surgical procedure to remove the womb (uterus). A hysterectomy alongside removal of endometriosis can reduce the risk of recurrence, according to Endometriosis UK, external.
In her blog, Barnett also said she suspected most of her pain may have been down to another condition, adenomyosis, which can be treated by a hysterectomy.
Her surgery was necessitated after she had an ultrasound while filming the final scene of the documentary, and a problem in her gallbladder was found. "Suddenly things became urgent and non negotiable."
The broadcaster added that she was hopeful that the surgery had helped.
She wrote: "Early indications are that the pain is very much improved - although I am still healing from the surgery itself so that also feels uncertain and frightening to admit - even to myself."

On the left, is Madalitso, a woman with a streak of pink in her hair, and a purple padded jacket over a fuchsia top. On the right is Chloe, who has red hair and wears a denim jacket.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/840f/live/8359ef10-5b70-11f1-8b8c-6d33e1d5abb6.jpg)

summary: BBC presenter Emma Barnett has revealed she underwent a hysterectomy and surgery for endometriosis just days before her documentary about the condition was broadcast. The 41-year-old broadcaster, who also had her gallbladder removed, described the timing as surreal and admitted she had the hysterectomy she never wanted to have. Barnett has since returned to Radio 4's Today programme and noted that early indications show her pain has improved.
key_points: Emma Barnett was hospitalized for a hysterectomy, extensive endometriosis surgery, and a gallbladder removal just 48 hours before her BBC Two documentary aired.
The surgery became urgent and non-negotiable after an ultrasound during the filming of the documentary's final scene revealed a problem with her gallbladder.
Barnett described the procedure as 'the hysterectomy I never wanted to have' and stated she felt blind-sided and robbed by the outcome.
Early indications show that her pain has improved, though she is still recovering from the surgery.

title: Charity complains about Channel 4 documentary examining ADHD
author: Ian Youngs
content:
![Promotional portrait photo of NHS psychiatrist Dr Max Pemberton looking at the camera](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/73a4/live/4dad13f0-9bf4-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
The documentary was presented by NHS psychiatrist Dr Max Pemberton
- Published
An ADHD charity has said it has complained to media regulator Ofcom about a Channel 4 documentary that suggested the condition is a myth.
The programme, titled The Great ADHD Myth?, was broadcast on Tuesday and its host, NHS psychiatrist Dr Max Pemberton, concluded it was "a social construct, not a disorder of the brain".
ADHD UK filed a complaint, saying: "ADHD is not a myth. It is not a social construct."
The Royal College of Psychiatrists also warned against "invalidating the condition".
Channel 4 defended the show, saying there is "considerable public debate on various aspects of ADHD" and it "is legitimate for that debate to be explored and for conventional understandings to be challenged".
The programme featured experts who are sceptical about ADHD and the way it is treated.
It also followed a 10-year-old boy who stopped his medication and made lifestyle changes to see how it affected his behaviour. The documentary ended with his mother saying he would stay off the drugs for the time being.
A caption at the end of the programme said the boy went back on his medication two months after filming and his school performance improved, but that he wanted to come off them again in the future.
ADHD UK said, external: "The programme's own end credits told you what its 60 minutes wouldn't: the boy at its centre went back on his medication, and his schoolwork improved.
"Their experiment disproved their conclusion. They aired their version anyway. We have already complained to Ofcom."
There was also criticism from Prof Subodh Dave, president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, external, who acknowledged that people "may have their own opinions about the diagnosis and treatment of ADHD", but said: "Invalidating the condition does a disservice to people with ADHD and professionals involved in their care."
He added: "The focus should be on improving access to high-quality assessments and care by addressing waiting lists that leave many people without vital support for years at a time, not questioning the legitimacy of a well-established neurodevelopmental disorder."
Another charity, ADHD Embrace, raised concerns with Channel 4 in advance, external, warning the programme risked "perpetuating misinformation about ADHD as a condition and discrimination against those families whose lives have been severely impacted by the condition".
In a statement, Channel 4 said: "This documentary does not deny the lived experience of those diagnosed with ADHD, but does present the view of an extensive range of senior medical experts - many of whom work or have worked with the NHS or have held presidential roles at professional membership bodies - who seek to question the conventional understanding of ADHD and if it is a neurodevelopmental condition.
"They also ask whether modern living has contributed to a rise in diagnoses, and whether there may be better alternatives for some children than medication."
The channel also said the programme sought to explore whether societal factors were contributing to the rise in diagnosis and medication, especially among boys.
Channel 4 said: "Whilst the film does not seek to provide answers from one family's experience, their experiences have opened up discussion around whether today's world is equipped to accommodate ADHD behaviours and the ethics of medicating these, particularly in children and particularly when the long-term effects remain unknown."
The Guardian called the programme "the most controversial show of the year", external, and its four-star review said the documentary "will incense and offend some of its viewers", but that "Pemberton answers his questions convincingly".
The Times also gave four stars, external, saying much of the documentary "felt convincing, or at least the start of a necessary discussion".
ADHD is described by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) , externalas "a behavioural syndrome characterised by hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention".
The NHS estimates, external that about 2.5 million people in England have ADHD, including those without a formal diagnosis.
Diagnosis rates of ADHD and autism have soared, and waiting lists for assessments on the NHS in England are at record levels, with lists even closing in some areas due to the huge demand.
Research from University College London suggests nearly a 20-fold increase in the number of UK adults diagnosed with ADHD between 2000 and 2018.
Despite these rises in diagnosis and referrals, some studies suggest ADHD is actually underdiagnosed.
In June, the Lancet Regional Health Europe journal published research suggesting that while around 1.2% of adults in England had an ADHD diagnosis, international prevalence data estimates it affects 3-5% of people. The authors of the study said this indicates it could still be under-diagnosed, particularly in older age groups.
summary: An ADHD charity has complained to Ofcom regarding a Channel 4 documentary titled The Great ADHD Myth?, presented by Dr Max Pemberton, which suggested the condition is a social construct rather than a brain disorder. The programme drew criticism from the Royal College of Psychiatrists and ADHD Embrace for invalidating a well-established condition, while Channel 4 defended the broadcast as a legitimate exploration of public debate surrounding ADHD. Despite the controversy and feature of a child stopping medication during filming, the documentary's own end credits noted that the boy subsequently returned to medication after his school performance declined.
key_points: ADHD UK filed an Ofcom complaint over the Channel 4 documentary presented by Dr Max Pemberton.
The Royal College of Psychiatrists warned against invalidating the condition and doing a disservice to patients.
Channel 4 defended the programme, stating it aimed to question conventional understandings and explore societal factors in rising diagnoses.
The documentary featured a 10-year-old boy who stopped taking medication, though end credits noted he returned to it two months later when his schoolwork suffered.

title: Hayden Panettiere latest: Heroes star’s on-off boyfriend was present at death scene
author: Jacob Stolworthy; Shahana Yasmin; Caitlin Hornik
content:
Hayden Panettiere, who became a household name as a teenager for her role in Heroes and later starred in Nashville and multiple Scream films, has died at age 36.
Panettiere was pronounced dead at a South Carolina apartment Sunday, August 16. A cause of death has not been revealed, but an autopsy showed no signs of trauma. Toxicology reports are pending and could take up to 12 weeks, according to the Greenville County Coroner’s Office.
A newly released incident report states that the 911 call was made by Brian Hickerson, 37, who is referred to as Panettiere’s boyfriend. He eportedly turned over a “bag of medication” belonging to Panettiere to the police, but the contents of that bag has so far been redacted. His brother Zach Hickerson was also present on the scene. The Independent has approached police for further information.
The actor’s father, Skip, confirmed Panettiere’s death in a heartbreaking statement to ABC News. Panettiere’s ex-fiance, Wladimir Klitschko said he was “deeply saddened” by the news but vowed to make sure the couple’s daughter, Kaya, “remembers the person” Panettiere was.
Dozens of Panettiere’s co-stars including Heroes actor Masi Oka, Nashville co-star Connie Britton, Tim Allen, Viola Davis and Melissa Barrera have offered heartfelt tributes to the two-time Golden Globe nominee on social media.
Among her most memorable roles were Sheryl Yoast in the 2000 Denzel Washington-led film Remember the Titans, high school cheerleader Claire Bennet on NBC’s sci-fi drama Heroes (2006-2010), and aspiring country singer Juliette Barnes on the hit TV series Nashville (2012-2018).
Her New York Times bestselling memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning, was published in May this year, in which she looked back at her childhood in Hollywood and her experiences with addiction, postpartum depression, abusive relationships, and the loss of custody of her daughter, Kaya, whom she shares with former heavyweight boxer Wladimir Klitschko.
Hayden Panettiere dead: Heroes and Nashville star dies aged 36
Hayden Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes, Nashville, and the Scream franchise, has died aged 36.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden,” Panettiere’s father, Skip said in a statement to ABC News. “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”
No cause of death was announced.
![Hayden Panettiere attends Jony And Marc's (RED) Auction at Sotheby's in New York](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/17/04/2026-08-17T031938Z_1937106696_RC230NATJBN1_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-HAYDEN-PANETTIERE.JPG)
Wladimir Klitschko breaks silence over ex-fiancée's death
In an Instagram post, Wladimir Klitschko wrote: “Our family is going through a time of profound shock and grief.
“The announcement of Hayden’s tragic death saddens me deeply. She left this world far too soon. Hayden was, although no longer my partner, an important part of my life and the mother of our daughter, Kaya.
“She built an incredible career through immense talent, while also facing the darker sides of a very demanding industry. Nothing will erase the times we shared or the place she had in our lives.
“To our daughter Kaya, I will always speak of her mother with respect and make sure she remembers the person she was.
“I extend my deepest condolences to Hayden’s parents, her friends, and her fans, who are also grieving today. Young and talented people like Hayden should not leave this world so soon.
“I ask everyone to please respect our family’s feelings and privacy during this incredibly difficult time. For now, this is all I wish to say.
“Thank you to everyone who is supporting my family and expressing their sincere condolences.
“Rest easy, Hayden. May you find eternal peace. #WeLoveYouHayden”
Panettiere still struggled with decades-old injuries
In her 2026 memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning, Panettiere recalled being thrown from a zebra while filming the 2005 movie, Racing Stripes.
Just 14 years old at the time, Panettiere suffered damage to two vertebrae in her neck, a concussion and severe whiplash.
“I kept my mouth shut and endured the pain in my back and neck,” she wrote in her memoir.
“Over 20 years later, these injuries still bother me.”
Cops spotted at Hickerson family home days after Panettiere's death
Police have been spotted at a Hickerson family residence about five miles from where Panettiere died Sunday.
Her on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach were both with her when she died.
Now, Page Six reported Wednesday that cops were seen outside a home belonging to the Hickerson brothers’ grandmother.
A pair of officers were seen around 8:20 a.m. ET knocking on front and side doors of the residence. They returned about 90 minutes later to “conduct a welfare check,” the outlet reported.
However, it was not clear who the intended target of the welfare check was.
The Independent has contacted the Greenville Police Department for more information.
Panettiere's 'Heroes' co-star says she 'knew every crew member’s name'
Sendhil Ramamurthy, who starred alongside the late actor on the NBC show Heroes, recalled Panettiere’s kindness.
“I learned a lot from her. She stuck up for background actors when they were mistreated, knew every crew member’s name, and was so generous with her time,” Ramamurthy wrote on Instagram.
“Sending love to her family, friends, and my fellow cast mates, RIP Hayd. You will be missed.”
Steven Tyler pays tribute to his 'dear friend'
The Aerosmith rocker and Panettiere partnered for a duet of the Patsy Cline song “Crazy” for a 2015 episode of Nashville.
Filmmaker recalls Panettiere's on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson being on movie set
Filmmaker Griff Furst worked with Panettiere on A Breed Apart, which was released in theaters in May 2025.
In an Instagram video shared August 17, Furst recalled Panettiere’s on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson being on set.
“I had met Hayden about 10 years before that and I knew that she was insanely talented, so when she signed on to do this picture that we were shooting, I was psyched. I really wanted to work with her. So I’m on set, and I get word from the movie’s security team who picked her up from the airport that something was off,” Furst said in the video.
“I didn’t think much about it, and so I left set and I walked over to greet her and her boyfriend Brian. He opened the door. Hayden was incredibly sweet and gracious and excited to work, but she was not okay,” he continued.
“I’m not going to get into the details of why that was, but having worked on over 100 movies and seeing just about everything, it was pretty clear that she wasn’t okay and the energy in her room was pretty dark.”
Baseball star's ties to Panettiere resurface
MLB star Pete Crow-Armstrong comes from a family of actors, including his mom, Ashley Crow, who played Hayden Panettiere’s mother on the hit NBC show Heroes.
The Chicago Cubs center fielder confessed his affection for Panettiere to NBC Chicago in a 2022 interview.
“Hayden Panettiere babysat me. I had the biggest crush on her,” Crow-Armstrong said. “Yeah, I’d say she was probably the coolest one for me.
“I liked being around the older actors, and I liked being babysat by my mom’s co-stars and whatnot.”
Jay Shetty is 'devastated and heartbroken' over Panettiere
Podcaster Shetty shared a tribute on social media Tuesday, months after he sat with Panettiere for what would turn out to be one of her final interviews.
“I’ve been devastated and heartbroken since I heard the news. I’m in shock and have been processing for the past day on your legacy and our loss,” he wrote.
“Just a few months ago, I had the privilege of sitting down with you on On Purpose. After the episode you told me it was truly healing. You said I was now like a big brother to you and that I helped you be brave,” he continued.
“But Hayden, you were the brave one. You were courageous, resilient, and so incredibly strong through so many difficult moments in your life. You should never have had to experience the things you did.”
Hayden Panettiere said she had 'a lot of life left to live'
In one of her last interviews with podcaster Jay Shetty in the months before her death, Hayden Panettiere spoke about her future with hope.
summary: Actor Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36 at a South Carolina apartment. An autopsy showed no signs of trauma, and the cause of death remains pending toxicological reports. Her on-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, and his brother were present at the scene when she passed away. Numerous co-stars and public figures have shared tributes honoring her life and career.
